A 79-year-old man has disabling pain from hip osteoarthritis. Oral NSAIDs were stopped after kidney injury, and nonpharmacologic and nonopioid treatments have provided inadequate relief. He is not a suitable surgical candidate and has never tried an opioid. Which drug should be tried before the other opioid options according to Hazzard's osteoarthritis chapter?

An 86-year-old woman has severe osteoarthritis involving all compartments of the knee. Persistent pain limits walking and social participation despite maximal pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic treatment. She is medically fit for surgery and wishes to discuss it. Which intervention is best supported?

A care-home resident with dementia and knee osteoarthritis cannot answer pain questions consistently and grimaces with movement. Staff report reduced activity. How should pain be assessed before treatment is adjusted?

An 83-year-old man with a painful, swollen knee undergoes arthrocentesis. The synovial fluid white blood cell count is 58,000 cells/mm3. In an evaluation for suspected osteoarthritis, how should this result be interpreted according to Hazzard?

An 80-year-old woman with end-stage knee osteoarthritis asks about knee replacement. She has COPD with FEV1 45% predicted, coronary disease with a stent placed two years ago, and continuous oxygen at 2 L. She lives in a two-story home and currently climbs the stairs on her hands and knees. Her cardiologist has cleared her for surgery. Which counseling principle about joint replacement is supported by Hazzard?

A 75-year-old woman reports impaired memory and difficulty managing finances that began after surgery and have persisted for four months. Assessment confirms cognitive decline without a current acute confusional state. Which term matches this time course in Hazzard?

An 82-year-old man with hip osteoarthritis and early frailty is referred for prehabilitation before surgery. Inadequate nutritional intake is also identified. Which program is consistent with Hazzard's approach to early frailty?

A 78-year-old woman taking warfarin reports a change in INR and use of a nonprescription cream bought online. A causal link has not been established. How should the cream be handled in medication review?

An 85-year-old man becomes confused on the second day after total knee arthroplasty. He pulls at his urinary catheter and fails to recognize his family. He has treated hypertension, normal serum chemistry and recent opioid exposure for postoperative pain. No focal neurologic signs or head trauma are found, and the catheter no longer has a clinical indication. Which action fits initial nonpharmacologic delirium management?
בת 79 בעלת כשרות שוקלת החלפת ברך אלקטיבית ומבקשת להבין את האפשרויות. איזה מידע על טיפולים חלופיים ועל היעדר טיפול נדרש לצורך הסכמה מדעת לפי סעיף 13 לחוק זכויות החולה?

An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease and knee osteoarthritis has recurrent falls and dizziness on standing, including two falls while reaching for his walker. He takes carbidopa–levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, and celecoxib 200 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 138/82 supine to 106/68 standing with dizziness. There is a moderate knee effusion. Which consideration supports reviewing the pramipexole dose as part of management?

An 84-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced dementia and hip osteoarthritis cries during routine care, moans during transfers, and resists bathing. Her PAINAD score is 7/10 despite scheduled acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. Her daughter, the health care proxy, fears opioid addiction. Which educational message about persistent pain in dementia is supported by Hazzard?

An older woman who walked before her fall has a displaced femoral-neck fracture. After assessment and consent, surgery is planned. Why is arthroplasty generally appropriate for this fracture according to Hazzard?

A 79-year-old man becomes acutely confused on the second day after hip hemiarthroplasty. He pulls at his catheter and does not recognize his wife, although he was alert and oriented the previous day. He has diabetes, mild cognitive impairment, and stage 4 CKD with an eGFR of 22 mL/min/1.73 m2. Temperature is 37.1°C, blood pressure 105/65, and heart rate 88. His medications include morphine PCA, enoxaparin 30 mg daily, and metformin 500 mg twice daily. During a complete delirium and medication assessment, which action specifically addresses the metformin contraindication in Hazzard?
An older woman with diagnosed depression starts mirtazapine after clinical assessment. Which combination of effects should be considered during follow-up?
A 76-year-old woman with dizziness on standing has orthostatic hypotension. A medication contributing to the problem has been identified. Which management principle is appropriate?

גבר בן 81 מגיע למעקב אמבולטורי 6 שבועות לאחר ניתוח לתיקון hip fracture. אשתו מדווחת שלעיתים הוא מבולבל, שוכח שיחות אחרונות אך זוכר אירועים מהעבר הרחוק בצורה תקינה. הוא מקבל ציון 24/30 ב-MMSE (איבד נקודות על recall ו-orientation). ה-MMSE שלו לפני ה-fracture היה 28/30. הוא סיים physical therapy ומהלך באופן עצמאי. CBC ופאנל מטבולי תקינים. רמת 25-hydroxyvitamin D היא 18 ng/mL. איזו התערבות הכי סביר שתשפר את תפקודו הקוגניטיבי?

An 85-year-old assisted-living resident with moderate Alzheimer disease is on day three after hip-fracture repair. After sleeping well on earlier nights, she is now awake, repeatedly getting out of bed, and saying she must get the children ready for school. She takes memantine 10 mg twice daily, vitamin D, acetaminophen as needed, and zolpidem 5 mg at bedtime added last night. Vital signs are normal. Which medication change follows Beers 2023 guidance for the new delirium?

A 77-year-old man in rehabilitation after hip-fracture repair has constant pain at rest and with movement. As-needed immediate-release oxycodone relieves it, but late administration allows pain to recur between doses. Which dosing strategy fits this pain pattern in Hazzard?
An 83-year-old woman regained independence after a hip fracture but avoids walking outside because she fears falling. Which possible sequence is described by Hazzard?

A 78-year-old man is admitted from primary care with three days of acute confusion, unsteadiness, and falls. Six weeks earlier he underwent right hip ORIF, complicated by postoperative delirium that resolved. Discharge medications included tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed and vitamin D 2000 IU daily. Laboratory results are Na 124, K 3.8, creatinine 1.1, and glucose 98. Which assessment of tramadol is supported by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

After rehabilitation for a hip fracture, a woman is independent in feeding and dressing. You now want to assess her ability to maintain an independent household. Which activities are instrumental activities of daily living?
A patient takes calcium carbonate as a calcium supplement. Which advice about administration and bowel effects agrees with Hazzard?
An 82-year-old long-term-care resident with cognitive impairment and urinary incontinence needs help toileting. The team wants a nighttime plan that protects sleep. Which approach follows Hazzard?

A 75-year-old woman is being reviewed for osteoporosis one year after a hip fracture. She completed five years of alendronate before the fracture. Her hip T-score is now −1.3, previously −2.9; calcium is 9.6 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m², and 25-hydroxyvitamin D 35 ng/mL. She has difficulty remembering daily medication but reliably attends a weekly bridge club. During discussion of treatment options, which drug binds RANKL to inhibit osteoclast activation?

An 88-year-old man in rehabilitation has lost weight and eats little. He dislikes his restrictive diet but eats preferred foods well. No swallowing disorder is found. Which food-based approach matches Hazzard recommendations for improving oral intake?
An 80-year-old woman has lost walking ability after hip-fracture repair and can participate in rehabilitation. What should guide selection of the rehabilitation setting after discharge?

An 84-year-old man is medically stable after a stroke and able to participate in rehabilitation. Assessment finds no delirium or active depression, but he struggles to see how exercises will help. He previously enjoyed woodworking. Which approach could help motivation according to Hazzard?
An older woman develops delirium after hip surgery. Alongside evaluation and treatment of medical causes, which environmental approach follows Hazzard?

An 81-year-old man in cardiac rehabilitation reports dizziness on standing. Assessment identifies several contributors, including medications and impaired vision. Which management principle is appropriate?

A 79-year-old woman with diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, and a recent L2 compression fracture is in skilled rehabilitation. She has progressed from a wheelchair to walking 100 ft with a walker but has had two near-falls while reaching. She leans heavily on the walker and has difficulty shifting weight sideways. HbA1c is 7.2% and vitamin D is 28 ng/mL. During review of exercise approaches, which description identifies tai chi as presented in Hazzard?

גבר בן 85 נמצא ביום 3 של שיקום אקוטי לאחר החלפת שני ברכיים. יש לו CKD stage 3 (eGFR 45), CHF (EF 40%), ואוסטאופורוזיס. הוא מוטיבציה אך מפתח כאב קשה (9/10) עם כיפוף הברך מעבר ל-70 מעלות, המגביל את התקדמות הטיפול. טיפול אנלגטי נוכחי: acetaminophen 1g TID, celecoxib 200mg יומי, oxycodone 5mg q6h PRN (משתמש ב-3-4 מנות ביום). אשתו שואלת על תרופות כאב חזקות יותר. מהי ההתאמה המתאימה ביותר?

A 77-year-old woman with dementia is undergoing rehabilitation after hip-fracture repair. She becomes agitated when staff move the affected limb and cannot answer pain questions consistently. Which approach is appropriate for assessing pain?

A man with Parkinson disease has recurrent rigidity before each levodopa dose, followed by a good response and no peak-dose dyskinesia. The team plans to alter the frequency of the same formulation before adding a drug. Which change fits wearing-off?
A 76-year-old woman starting resistance training reports severe muscle soreness and prolonged generalized fatigue after each session. How should this affect the next exercise prescription?
An 83-year-old woman with COPD experiences dyspnea during rehabilitation. Which breathing modification is described in Hazzard as a way to reduce the sensation of breathlessness?
An older adult treated with insulin develops impaired vision and hand dexterity. Before selecting a self-monitoring device, what should be assessed according to Hazzard?

An 86-year-old woman with dementia has difficulty remembering exercises during rehabilitation after a fracture. She cooperates with guidance, and her daughter wishes to help. Which approach should guide rehabilitation goals?

A 78-year-old man with postoperative iron-deficiency anemia stopped an adequate oral iron regimen because of substantial intolerance. He is stable and has no active bleeding. Which method of iron replacement is supported by Hazzard?
An 81-year-old woman in rehabilitation after a pelvic fracture practices transfers and balance. Which goal describes a functional outcome in daily life rather than a measure of exercise performance?

גבר בן 77 עם פרקינסון ודיספאגיה מבין את סיכון האספירציה ואת חלופות ההזנה, ומסוגל לקבל החלטה. הוא מבקש לאכול דרך הפה, ואשתו מתנגדת. אין מצב חירום ואין החלטה המתירה חריגה מכללי ההסכמה. לפי סעיף 13 לחוק זכויות החולה, על בחירתו של מי יש לבסס את ההחלטה לאחר מסירת המידע?
During a preoperative assessment, the team plans to use the Clinical Frailty Scale. Which description matches the scale in Hazzard?

An 84-year-old man in rehabilitation after hip surgery develops acute confusion and stops participating in therapy. Renal impairment and electrolyte disturbances are present, and he is receiving an opioid. Which management approach is appropriate?

A woman after a stroke can transfer to a commode, but cognitive impairment prevents her from requesting help in time. There are no signs of infection or urinary retention. Staff are available to help. Which intervention is appropriate?

An older adult has persistent pain after orthopedic surgery that worsens during physical therapy. A surgical complication has been excluded. Which pain-regimen plan matches Hazzard's approach to supporting rehabilitation?
A 77-year-old woman has iron-deficiency anemia. Which follow-up finding supports changing to intravenous iron under the recommendations in Hazzard’s anemia chapter?

An opioid-naive 85-year-old woman with dementia and chronic kidney disease has persistent pain limiting rehabilitation despite nonopioid treatment. After assessment, a trial of an opioid is chosen. Which initiation principle matches Hazzard?

A person with Parkinson disease responds well to each levodopa dose, but stiffness and slowness recur before each daytime dose. There is no significant dyskinesia. The initial plan is to adjust the timing of the existing formulation. Which change addresses this end-of-dose problem?

An 82-year-old woman develops inattention, confusion, and fluctuating alertness after hip surgery. Gabapentin appears on her medication list, but its start date and any recent dose changes are unknown. Which diagnostic approach is appropriate?

A 76-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and chronic back pain has become sedentary and mentally foggy despite physical therapy. He takes duloxetine, cyclobenzaprine, and acetaminophen. Which medication change removes a skeletal muscle relaxant that the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria recommend avoiding in older adults?
An 83-year-old woman with systolic heart failure is receiving spironolactone. Which monitoring pair is especially important during initiation and dose titration because of this drug’s risks?

A 79-year-old man is undergoing rehabilitation after a severe illness. Nutritional assessment identifies unintentional weight loss and inadequate energy and protein intake. An oral nutritional supplement is added to meals and rehabilitation. How should it be incorporated to increase daily intake?
אישה בת 80 עם פרקינסון לאחר שבר ירך מתקדמת לאט בשיקום. המשפחה מבקשת לדעת כיצד יוחלט על המשך התוכנית ועל השחרור. מה נדרש לפי חוזר משרד הבריאות?

An older adult with stable type 2 diabetes is being considered for oral treatment. There is no acute illness, unstable heart failure, or renal contraindication. Which statement describes the principal glucose-lowering action of metformin in Hazzard?

A woman with dementia and a painful fracture continues to show signs of pain despite an adequate trial of acetaminophen. What can be considered next under the stepwise pain-treatment approach described in Hazzard?

A 75-year-old man with COPD presents for pulmonary rehabilitation. His oxygen saturation is 92% at rest and 86% while walking. According to Hazzard, which additional finding supports oxygen use during exertion in this setting?
An 81-year-old woman with low vision from macular degeneration is practicing stair climbing in rehabilitation. Which environmental adjustment will help her identify the step edges?

A 78-year-old man with dementia and falls takes oxybutynin. The team decides to remove the strongly anticholinergic drug from his regimen and plan treatment of urinary incontinence separately. Which action achieves that aim?

An 84-year-old woman has dysuria and urinary frequency without fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms. Creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Urine culture grows E. coli susceptible to nitrofurantoin, ciprofloxacin, and amoxicillin-clavulanate but resistant to TMP-SMX. Which oral agent is the appropriate first-line choice for acute simple cystitis according to Hazzard?
For which stage of Alzheimer disease does Hazzard explicitly describe an approved indication for memantine?
A woman with dementia becomes restless during bathing. There is no immediate danger, and behavioral intervention has not yet been tried. Which initial approach is appropriate?

A man with Alzheimer disease and diabetes receives basal insulin once daily but makes dosing errors and sometimes misses meals. His daughter can help. Which adjustment directly addresses safe implementation of his existing regimen?

אישה בת 83 עם דמנציה מתקדמת מסוג אלצהיימר (MMSE 8/30) מאושפזת מבית אבות עם דלקת ריאות משאיפה. היא ירדה 15% ממשקל גופה במהלך 6 חודשים וזקוקה לסיוע מלא בהאכלה. היא אינה מזהה עוד את בני משפחתה. בהערכה של ריפוי בעיסוק או קלינאות תקשורת תועדה הפרעת בליעה חמורה עם שאיפת נוזלים דקים. בנה שואל לגבי הכנסת צינור הזנה. בהנחיות המקדימות שלה נכתב שהיא מסרבת להזנה מלאכותית. איזו תגובה מתייחסת בצורה הטובה ביותר למטרות הטיפול?

A woman with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis has not yet tried an anti-inflammatory medication and wants topical treatment before an oral drug. Which rationale supports topical diclofenac according to Hazzard?

An 80-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia and atrial fibrillation is reviewed after a mechanical fall at home. His wife reports increasing confusion over the past two weeks and difficulty managing medications. He takes warfarin with a target INR of 2-3, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. His INR today is 4.8, without active bleeding. After addressing the current INR abnormality, the clinician is considering a direct oral anticoagulant for longer-term stroke prevention. Which principle should guide this assessment?
A woman with dementia develops confusion and hallucinations over several days after starting a sleep medication. She poses no danger to herself. What is the appropriate initial approach?

A patient with delirium and severe agitation has not improved with nonpharmacologic measures. After assessment, cautious antipsychotic treatment is selected. What is the clinical treatment endpoint described in Hazzard?
מטופלת מאושפזת בישראל מוגדרת חסרת ישע. בבירור עולה חשד שהאדם האחראי עליה פוגע בה. איזה צעד מתחייב לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות?

A 75-year-old man wakes several times at night to urinate. Before changing medication, the clinician wants to assess whether increased nighttime urine production contributes to the symptom. Which record would help?
What did the controlled study described by Hazzard find about mirtazapine in patients with dementia and sleep disturbances?

A 79-year-old woman with dementia and chronic constipation develops acute abdominal pain. CT has demonstrated colonic perforation around a hard fecal mass, and examination shows peritonitis. Which approach is appropriate?
A patient with chronic kidney disease takes spironolactone and develops non-life-threatening hyperkalemia. Which approach addresses a reversible contributor to the potassium elevation?

An 84-year-old man with dementia develops acute confusion, inattention, and visual hallucinations; his CAM assessment is positive. He is calm, not markedly distressed, cooperates with care, and poses no danger to himself or others. Evaluation for reversible contributors has begun. What is the appropriate initial symptom-management approach?
A woman with mild dementia dresses independently but makes medication errors. What is the appropriate conclusion for a home-safety assessment?

An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease has persistent cognitive decline after reversible acute and medication-related contributors have been excluded. The current goal is to treat cognitive symptoms. Which medication class is described in Hazzard as useful for this goal?

אישה בישראל נקבעה כחולה הנוטה למות, אך לא כחולה בשלב סופי. היא אינה בעלת כשרות, סובלת סבל משמעותי ורצונה שלא להאריך את חייה נקבע כדין. לצד החלטה להימנע מהחייאה בהתאם לרצונה, אובחנה דלקת ריאות שהרופא קבע שאינה קשורה כלל למחלתה חשוכת המרפא. כיצד יש להתייחס לטיפול השגרתי בדלקת הריאות לפי סעיף 16?

An 85-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 14) and osteoarthritis has fallen twice in the past month without injury. She inconsistently uses a walker. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg four times daily; amitriptyline 25 mg nightly was added for sleep six weeks ago. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 72 to 78. Which action directly addresses the recently added tricyclic antidepressant as a possible contributor?

A 78-year-old man with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer disease, MMSE 20, and stage 3 CKD with eGFR 42 repeatedly asks questions and follows his wife around the home. She is exhausted and considering institutional care. He takes memantine 10 mg twice daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg; examination and vital signs are unremarkable. Which plan provides caregiver respite and meaningful activity as described in Hazzard?

An 82-year-old woman with mixed Alzheimer and vascular dementia, MMSE 16, and hypertension has been more confused for two weeks. She cannot clearly describe symptoms. She is afebrile, with blood pressure 156/84 mm Hg and pulse 78/min. She takes donepezil 10 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly, started three weeks ago for sleep. Basic laboratory tests are normal except creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, previously 1.0. Which change directly reduces a first-generation antihistamine's anticholinergic burden?

A woman with dementia with Lewy bodies develops rigidity and reduced responsiveness after receiving haloperidol. Which susceptibility described in Hazzard warrants concern about an adverse drug reaction?

An 83-year-old man taking gabapentin has a creatinine clearance of 24 mL/min and develops somnolence. Which principle does the 2023 Beers renal-function table give for gabapentin in impaired kidney function?

A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease becomes restless in the afternoon and wanders around her home. There is no aggression, psychosis, or immediate danger. Evaluation identifies no acute illness or unmet physical need, and behavioral intervention has not been tried. What is the appropriate initial approach?

גבר בן 86 עם דמנציה מעורבת (MMSE 15), CHF (EF 35%), ו-CKD שלב 3b מאושפז עם CHF לא מאוזנת. הוא מבולבל לגבי מיקום ותאריך אך מזהה בני משפחה. לבתו יש ייפוי כוח מתמשך והיא מציינת שהוא היה רוצה 'הכל'. הוא נוטל furosemide 40mg BID, carvedilol 12.5mg BID, lisinopril 5mg, ו-memantine 10mg BID. לאחר דיורזה, מצבו יציב. טיפול פליאטיבי ממליץ על הוספיס. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?

אישה בת 77 עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה (MoCA 23) ויתר לחץ דם מופנית בשל תלונות על זיכרון. שכחה שני תורים אצל רופא ואיבדה את הדרך בנסיעה לבית אחותה (ביקור חודשי שנמשך שנים). מנהלת כספים ותרופות באופן עצמאי. הבת מבקשת 'כדורים לזיכרון.' תרופות נוכחיות: lisinopril 20mg, HCTZ 12.5mg. לחץ דם 138/82. בדיקות מעבדה מראות B12 תקין, TSH תקין. איזו התערבות הכי מתאימה?
למטופל עם קיהיון שהוגדר כנוטה למות יש קושי באכילה, אך טרם בוצעה הערכה מקצועית של הבליעה והצרכים התזונתיים. מהו צעד המתאים להמלצות הוועדה הלאומית על הזנה?

A woman with dementia and urinary incontinence needs a behavioral alternative after medication was stopped because of adverse effects. She cooperates with care but cannot keep a diary or remember exercises. A caregiver is available during the day. What defines scheduled toileting?

A 75-year-old woman with early Alzheimer disease (MMSE 24) and diabetes attends a routine review. She lives alone, drives short distances, and uses a pillbox filled weekly by her daughter. HbA1c is 9.2%, compared with 7.8% six months earlier. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and glipizide 10 mg twice daily. Her daughter has found glucose tablets around the home and reports morning shakiness. During a review of possible hypoglycemia, which change removes a hypoglycemia-risk drug while individualizing her treatment goals?

An 85-year-old man with dementia, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes develops new confusion and inattention over one day. His family describes a clear change from his usual state. Initial assessment also shows hypotension and deterioration in renal function. Which approach to identifying the causes of delirium is supported by Hazzard?

A 78-year-old woman develops CAM-positive delirium after hip-fracture surgery, pulling at her catheter and trying to leave bed. She was independent in instrumental activities before admission. Her medications include oxycodone, famotidine, and enoxaparin; renal function has worsened and sodium is low. Alongside identifying and treating contributors, which care plan follows Hazzard?

An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer dementia has become more confused over three days. He lives in assisted living and has a baseline MMSE of 19/30. He accused staff of stealing a wallet later found in his drawer and now reports seeing children who are not present. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Temperature is 36.8 degrees C, BP 140/85, and heart rate 78; urine shows 10-20 white cells and positive nitrites. Which feature most directly distinguishes the current change from his baseline dementia?

A 92-year-old nursing-home resident with severe Alzheimer disease, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease has persistent aggression during care. Hypokalemia has been corrected and acute medical causes addressed. After nonpharmacologic measures fail, the team considers a nonemergency medication trial. She already takes citalopram at the chapter’s maximum daily dose. Which plan follows Hazzard’s guidance?

A 79-year-old man develops inattention and fluctuating confusion after starting a new medication. He has no fever, focal neurologic deficit, or dangerous agitation. Evaluation identifies the medication as a possible contributor. Which management principle is appropriate?

An 86-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter and needs help with IADLs. On the third hospital day for pneumonia she is more confused at night, sleeps during the day, is oriented to person, and picks at unseen objects. CAM is positive. She receives ceftriaxone 1 g daily and acetaminophen as needed. Alongside evaluating and treating causes, which environmental approach is consistent with delirium and sleep-wake management?

A 77-year-old man remains mechanically ventilated in the ICU five days after CABG. He appears awake but follows commands inconsistently; his wife reports that he seems unlike himself. Preoperative MMSE was 28/30. He receives fentanyl 50 mcg/hour, propofol 30 mcg/kg/min during weaning, and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. Which CAM adaptation is specifically described for ICU assessment using nonverbal tasks?

An 83-year-old woman has a COPD exacerbation with acute hypercarbia and respiratory acidosis. She is a candidate for noninvasive positive pressure ventilation and has no contraindication. What is the role of this treatment?
An older patient with severe persistent pain is being considered for opioid analgesia. Which principle is appropriate when starting treatment in an older adult?

A 76-year-old woman takes gabapentin for neuropathic pain. Following kidney injury, her calculated creatinine clearance is 38 mL/min and she develops drowsiness and confusion. Alongside assessment of her altered mental status, which gabapentin adjustment follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
An 88-year-old man with Parkinson disease and established visual hallucinations is assessed for possible new delirium. Which finding provides the most direct support for its core features?
A woman is transferred to postacute care after hospitalization while still delirious. What prognostic association does Hazzard describe for persistent delirium?
An older adult started oral diphenhydramine for sleep and subsequently developed confusion. Which consideration belongs in the medication review according to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
A patient with delirium has several possible precipitants, including a medication change, an electrolyte disturbance, and acute illness. How should treatment address these factors?
בישראל, חולה הנוטה למות סובל למרות טיפול מקל. הוצע טיפול נוסף התואם את רצונו ואת עקרונות הטיפול המקל, אך כרוך בסיכון סביר לחייו. מה קובע החוק?

An 84-year-old woman with stable dementia develops inattention and fluctuating confusion over one day. She has no fever or focal neurologic deficit; glucose and electrolytes are normal, and an initial assessment for infection and volume status has been performed. Her initial delirium evaluation is ongoing. Which action belongs in the routine initial evaluation?
גבר בן 79 בישראל עם דמנציה מוקדמת אובד בדרכים מוכרות ומתעקש להמשיך לנהוג. לאחר הערכה הרופא סבור שמחלתו מסכנת אותו בנהיגה ומחליט שיש צורך בדיווח למרב״ד. מה עליו לעשות עד להערכת המרב״ד?

An 81-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment asks about exercise. How does the review Dementia Prevention and Treatment distinguish the evidence for dementia prevention from the evidence for cognitive improvement with exercise that includes strength training?

A 76-year-old man newly diagnosed with Alzheimer disease (MMSE 21) wanders at night, accuses his wife of infidelity, and becomes agitated during personal care. His wife, the primary caregiver, has slept no more than three hours a night for weeks. She asks about nursing-home care but recalls promising never to place him there. Which intervention directly provides temporary relief from her caregiving duties?

An 85-year-old patient with moderate Alzheimer disease takes immediate-release memantine 10 mg twice daily. Calculated creatinine clearance is 24 mL/min. Which adjustment follows the dosing table in Hazzard?
בבית חולים בישראל עולה חשד לפגיעה באישה מבוגרת המגיעה עם בן משפחה. לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות, מהו צעד הבירור הראשוני המתאים?

An 82-year-old man with vascular dementia is hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure. He is usually oriented to person but now fails to recognize his daughter, has difficulty sustaining attention, and was awake overnight trying to catch a bus. Which interpretation best fits the acute mental-status change?
מטופלת הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות שאינה בעלת כשרות. אין הנחיות מקדימות, ייפוי כוח או החלטת ועדה. בני המשפחה חלוקים לגבי רצונה. מה רלוונטי לרופא האחראי בבירור רצונה לפי סעיף 5(ג)?
An 80-year-old man with lower urinary tract symptoms and postural dizziness takes terazosin. Why might a selective alpha blocker such as tamsulosin be considered?
חולה עם דמנציה הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות, אך מסוגלת לקבל מזון ונוזלים בכמות מספקת דרך הפה בעזרת התאמות. איזו דרך הזנה מועדפת בהמלצות המותב?

A 78-year-old woman with early Alzheimer disease still cooks at home. Her daughter has found a burner left on twice; medication administration is already supervised. What addresses the reported safety risk?

An 81-year-old man with vascular dementia becomes agitated during evening dressing assistance but sleeps well once in bed. His wife gives diphenhydramine during agitation. No immediate threat of substantial harm is identified, and behavioral measures have not been tried. Which initial approach follows the Beers Criteria?

אישה בת 77 עם mild cognitive impairment וסוכרת מגיעה עם בעלה, שמדווח שהיא ביצעה רכישות מרובות באינטרנט של פריטים שאינה צריכה, בסך כולל של $3,000 בחודש האחרון. היא אינה זוכרת את הרכישות. ה-MMSE שלה הוא 25/30 עם ליקוי בזיכרון ובתפקוד ניהולי. HbA1c הוא 7.2%. MRI מראה שינויים קלים ב-periventricular white matter. מהו הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?
During a sleep study in an 84-year-old man with dementia, which combination of airflow and respiratory effort identifies a central apneic event?

A 79-year-old man with longstanding Parkinson disease develops cognitive decline and visual hallucinations while taking carbidopa-levodopa, ropinirole, and amantadine. During medication review, which description of amantadine is supported by Hazzard?

An 84-year-old woman with cognitive decline takes tolterodine. Her family asks whether less emphasis on this drug than on oxybutynin means that cognitive risk can be disregarded. What follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

A 77-year-old man with early Parkinson disease lives alone and independently manages his IADLs. His daughter requests power of attorney because she believes he has dementia. He has mild rest tremor, cogwheeling, and bradykinesia. MoCA is 24/30 with visuospatial and executive errors, but he accurately describes his medicines, manages finances online, and drives safely. Which response addresses the discrepancy between cognitive screening and function?

אישה בת 81 עם דמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר מתקדמת-בינונית (FAST שלב 6a) ופרקינסון מתקדם מאושפזת עקב דלקת ריאות אספירטיבית. היא כרותת מיטה, זקוקה לסיוע בהאכלה, וסבלה מ-3 דלקות ריאה ב-6 חודשים. CXR מראה קונסולידציה באונה התחתונה מימין. המשפחה שואלת לגבי הנחת PEG. ההנחיות המקדימות שלה קובעות 'לא לתזונה מלאכותית.' מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?

An 85-year-old man with mild Parkinson disease and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) develops visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg twice daily and pramipexole 0.5 mg three times daily. Vital signs and head CT are normal. Which medication-review conclusion follows Hazzard's comparison of dopamine agonists with levodopa?

A 78-year-old woman with asymmetric tremor and bradykinesia is reassessed after a previous diagnosis of essential tremor. Tremor is prominent when her hand rests and lessens with voluntary movement. Which interpretation matches the source?

An 82-year-old man with dementia and parkinsonism develops acute confusion, rigidity, and fever after a medication change. During review of medication-related hyperthermia, which pairing correctly describes neuroleptic and anticholinergic effects in Hazzard?
A 76-year-old woman develops compulsive gambling and shopping after starting pramipexole. After discussing the connection to treatment, which medication-adjustment principle is described by Hazzard?
A man with longstanding Parkinson disease who takes dopaminergic medication develops orthostatic hypotension. Which interpretation matches Hazzard?
An older woman is starting tramadol. Which sodium-monitoring plan follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria when treatment is started or its dosage changes?
A 79-year-old man with Parkinson disease dementia will start oral rivastigmine after assessment of suitability. Which initiation strategy matches the approach described in Hazzard?
An older woman with Parkinson disease receives amantadine to reduce dyskinesias. Which adverse effect explains difficulty tolerating the drug in older adults according to Hazzard?

A 77-year-old woman with mild parkinsonism and type 2 diabetes has six months of worsening short-stepped gait and difficulty initiating movement, without tremor. MRI shows enlarged ventricles and periventricular white-matter changes. Carbidopa-levodopa provides little benefit. CSF opening pressure is 180 mm H2O. In Hazzard’s differential of parkinsonism, which diagnosis is specifically associated with the enlarged-ventricle finding?

An 81-year-old man with progressive dementia has prominent fluctuations in attention, recurrent visual hallucinations, and bradykinesia with rigidity. How should this combination be interpreted when assessing dementia with Lewy bodies?

An 84-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia and diabetes is transferred from her nursing home after developing increased confusion and falls over two days. Mirtazapine 15 mg nightly was started a week ago for depression and poor appetite. She is somnolent, with blood pressure falling from 140/80 supine to 110/65 standing and mild cogwheeling. Sodium is 128 mEq/L, glucose 180 mg/dL, and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. Which mirtazapine-related risk and monitoring approach is supported by Beers 2023?

A 78-year-old man with a two-year history of behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia is brought by his daughter for worsening aggression, with compulsive food-taking and inappropriate sexual comments at his nursing facility. Yesterday he pushed another resident who tried to stop him taking dessert. He has hypertension and osteoarthritis, takes lisinopril 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and has an MMSE score of 22/30. Which statement about treatment of the compulsive behavior is supported by Hazzard?

An 81-year-old woman has progressive word-finding difficulty and trouble naming familiar objects. She uses nonspecific words such as 'things' and has fluent speech with semantic paraphasias, intact grammar, and preserved repetition. She still manages finances and drives safely. Her history includes diabetes and chronic kidney disease. MRI shows asymmetric left temporal atrophy. Which syndrome best fits this language-led presentation?
For a patient with Parkinson disease and cognitive impairment, which drug is described in Hazzard as useful for cognitive symptoms? Two options are valid; either is accepted.

An older female care-home resident with new delirium is hemodynamically stable, with no fever or localizing urinary symptoms. A urine culture is positive, and no invasive urologic procedure is planned. Which approach is consistent with Hazzard?

A 76-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment develops apathy, stops attending his weekly poker games, loses interest in his grandchildren’s activities, and becomes upset when his fixed breakfast routine changes. MMSE is 26/30, and MRI shows bilateral frontal atrophy. His son asks about familial dementia. Among these genetic changes, which is linked in Hazzard to younger-onset Alzheimer disease rather than being one of the genetic causes discussed in its section on frontotemporal dementia?

An older woman with delirium remains dangerously agitated despite treatment of contributing causes and nonpharmacologic measures. A brief antipsychotic trial is chosen. Which target describes the limited clinical role of the drug in Hazzard?

A 79-year-old woman has progressive aphasia with fluent speech, loss of word meaning, and surface dyslexia. Sentence repetition is relatively preserved. Which imaging pattern supports semantic variant primary progressive aphasia?

An older man has progressive bulbar symptoms, upper and lower motor neuron signs, and behavioral changes. He is diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Which effect of riluzole is described in Hazzard?

A 77-year-old woman develops a poorly controlled right arm over one year. She drops objects, and the arm sometimes grasps her clothes involuntarily. She has difficulty planning meals and operating the microwave. Examination shows asymmetric right-arm rigidity and dystonia, cortical sensory loss, and ideomotor apraxia. MRI shows asymmetric left frontoparietal atrophy. Six months of carbidopa-levodopa has not helped. Which clinical syndrome best describes this combination?

An 83-year-old man with Alzheimer disease has begun hoarding newspapers and repeatedly checking the mailbox. Delirium and untreated pain have been excluded. He has no major depression, dangerous psychosis, or aggression that threatens anyone's safety. The family has not tried behavioral strategies. What is the first step?

A 75-year-old woman with behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia is referred for genetic counseling. Relatives have FTD and ALS. Which gene does the chapter identify as the major cause of familial FTD, ALS, and their combined phenotype?

An 84-year-old man develops dizziness, falls, and an orthostatic blood pressure drop after starting tamsulosin. Initial evaluation finds no urinary retention, volume depletion, or acute cardiac cause. What is the appropriate initial medication approach?

אישה בת 78 עם FTD מסוג התנהגותי שאובחנה לפני שנתיים מובאת על ידי המשפחה בשל החמרה בהתנהגות. היא הושעתה מתפקידה כמתנדבת בספרייה בשל אכילת חטיפים של מבקרים והערות מיניות. אתמול נמצאה עירומה במסדרון הבניין. היא גרה לבד ומסרבת לעזרה ב-IADLs למרות מזון מקולקל במקרר. תרופות נוכחיות: sertraline 100 mg ביום שהוחל לפני שישה חודשים. לבתה יש ייפוי כוח בר-קיימא לצרכי רפואה. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?

An 81-year-old man has a year of progressive, effortful, telegraphic speech with grammatical errors. Single-word comprehension is preserved. He has mild right-arm weakness, and MRI shows left frontal atrophy involving the inferior frontal region. His wife reports a diagnosis of depression two years ago after social withdrawal and loss of interest in golf. The language syndrome suggests nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia. Which additional finding would specifically suggest an associated corticobasal motor syndrome?

A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis has three years of worsening word finding and getting lost while driving. Her MMSE is 22/30, with losses in orientation, recall, and naming. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily; eGFR is 52 mL/min. While considering donepezil, the clinician reviews chronic naproxen use. Which statement supports reconsidering naproxen under Beers 2023?

A 76-year-old man taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation has a traumatic subdural hematoma after a fall. He develops confusion, but repeat CT shows no enlargement. Which intervention specifically reverses the warfarin effect, rather than investigating or treating another possible cause of confusion?
An 84-year-old woman with epilepsy, cognitive impairment, and medical comorbidities needs an antiseizure medication. Which principle should guide selection according to Hazzard?

A 79-year-old former boxer develops behavioral and cognitive changes. His family asks how chronic traumatic encephalopathy is definitively diagnosed according to Hazzard. Which type of evidence supports the definitive diagnosis described in the source?
An 81-year-old man taking tamsulosin for prostatic urinary symptoms develops urinary retention during hospitalization. After bladder drainage, which principle should guide further management?
אישה בישראל עם דמנציה מתונה שמונה לה אפוטרופוס זקוקה להחלטה על המשך בירור רפואי לאחר נפילה. ניתן לברר את דעתה באמצעות הסבר מותאם. בתה מבקשת לצמצם טיפול. מה נדרש מהאפוטרופוס לפני ההחלטה?

An 82-year-old man with Parkinson disease (Hoehn-Yahr stage 3) is hospitalized after a backward fall with head injury; CT shows no acute finding. On day two his MoCA is 22/30, compared with 25/30 three months earlier. He is more confused in the evening and sees children in the room. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily and pramipexole 1 mg three times daily. Alongside evaluation for acute causes, which medication-review approach addresses a recognized contributor to hallucinations?

A 78-year-old woman sustains a nonpenetrating head injury in a fall. Loss of consciousness lasts 10 minutes, posttraumatic amnesia lasts 3 hours, and the initial GCS is 14. How is the injury classified?

An 85-year-old man develops delirium after hospitalization following a fall. After assessment and treatment of acute causes, he is stable, settles with reorientation, and neither endangers anyone nor disrupts essential treatment. Which intervention is appropriate now?
A former contact-sport athlete develops memory and behavioral changes, raising concern for chronic traumatic encephalopathy. According to Hazzard, what is required for a definitive diagnosis?
An 80-year-old woman with postoperative back pain and chronic neuropathic pain is receiving an opioid. The team considers adding gabapentin. Which risk explains caution with the combination?

An 83-year-old man with CKD and a remote traumatic brain injury from a motorcycle accident at age 25 presents after his first seizure. His wife reports progressive forgetfulness over two years. EEG shows left temporal sharp waves; MRI shows left mesial temporal sclerosis and old right frontal encephalomalacia. His calculated creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. If levetiracetam is selected, which renal prescribing approach follows Table 6 of the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
A 79-year-old woman has functional decline, cognitive complaints, and significant depressive symptoms after a mild head injury. Which principle should guide assessment and treatment?

An 81-year-old woman with diabetes and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) is hospitalized after a fall. CT shows a thin acute subdural hematoma, and neurosurgery recommends observation. Her medications include metformin 500 mg twice daily, glipizide 5 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Glucose is 250–300 mg/dL on hospital day 2. The team selects basal insulin for glycemic control. Which plan follows the renal and insulin guidance in Hazzard?
An older adult who was independent in bathing and dressing now needs help with both. Which interpretation is consistent with Hazzard?

An 84-year-old man is admitted after a high-speed motor vehicle collision with brief loss of consciousness. GCS is 15, and CT shows small frontal contusions. His history includes professional boxing in his thirties and forties, hypertension, and recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment. He takes donepezil 10 mg and lisinopril 20 mg. On hospital day three he becomes agitated and paranoid, accusing staff of poisoning him. Which pattern would support an acute delirium syndrome?
A 78-year-old man taking an SSRI develops hyponatremia. Urine osmolality is inappropriately high for the low serum sodium. How should this finding be interpreted according to Hazzard?
An 84-year-old woman with advanced lung disease says that she wants her life to end. How should questions about suicide be approached according to Hazzard?

A 76-year-old man has well-formed visual hallucinations and spontaneous parkinsonism. Dementia with Lewy bodies is being considered. What additional finding is needed to meet the dementia component of the diagnosis?
After shared discussion, an older woman whose condition is stable begins a gradual venlafaxine taper. New symptoms appear during dose reduction. How should they be interpreted?

A 73-year-old man is evaluated for delusions and hallucinations. After medical evaluation and medication review, the decision is made to start an antipsychotic. There is no immediate danger requiring urgent sedation. Compared with a younger patient, what starting-dose and titration approach is recommended?

An 88-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate Alzheimer disease has become withdrawn over two months, no longer joins enjoyable activities, needs prompting to eat and spends much of the day in bed. He has lost weight despite no identified acute illness. He takes donepezil, memantine and docusate. Assessment has not identified major depression, dangerous psychosis or aggression. Which initial approach fits management of neuropsychiatric symptoms?
During a safety review of lithium in an older patient with dementia, which characteristic explains concern about confusion and falls during treatment?

An 82-year-old man with mild dementia and treated depression has acquired a firearm for protection. His wife recently found him looking sad while holding the loaded gun. He denies suicidal thoughts and says he was checking the weapon. He takes sertraline and donepezil. Alongside immediate assessment of suicide risk, which action directly reduces access to lethal means?
A 77-year-old woman takes lithium. An ACE inhibitor or a loop diuretic is being considered. What shared concern does Beers 2023 identify for these combinations?

A 74-year-old woman with depression and osteoarthritis has persistent hip pain despite acetaminophen. She takes sertraline and declines NSAIDs because of gastrointestinal concerns. The team is considering a supervised change to duloxetine. Which source-described action explains its potential analgesic role?

An 80-year-old man develops delirium during admission for a heart-failure exacerbation. Medication review identifies trazodone, prescribed for sleep, as a potentially harmful contributor without a current essential indication. Which medication strategy follows Hazzard's approach?

A 75-year-old man remains worried about serious heart disease after an unrevealing evaluation, repeatedly checks his pulse, and avoids activity. Psychotherapy for illness anxiety is being considered. Which psychotherapy modality does Hazzard describe as the most rigorously studied for anxiety disorders?

An 83-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension improved after escitalopram treatment for major depression. She now reports falls and cognitive symptoms, and medication review raises concern about adverse effects. After reassessing benefits and risks, she and her clinician decide to discontinue treatment without an emergency indication for abrupt cessation. Which follow-up plan follows Hazzard?

A 78-year-old man gradually develops changes in personality and social judgment. Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia is being considered. Which early profile would support that diagnosis according to Hazzard?

A 72-year-old woman has severe depression, reduced food intake and function, and limited response to several medication trials. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is being considered. Which information is consistent with Hazzard?
A 78-year-old man is diagnosed with major depression. After discussion, he chooses medication, and sertraline is selected. Which principle for initiation and follow-up agrees with Hazzard?

An 84-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis and recurrent urinary infections develops agitation, visual hallucinations and insomnia after starting ciprofloxacin for dysuria. She also takes donepezil, calcium with vitamin D and regular alprazolam. Which medication-review principle should guide assessment of her acute confusion?

A 79-year-old man with depression, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and chronic pain reports worsening mood and poor sleep six months after his wife's death. He drinks three to four glasses of wine nightly to sleep. He takes sertraline 100 mg daily, started four months ago, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime. His PHQ-9 score is 22. Which approach directly addresses the two sleep self-treatments that Hazzard identifies as problematic in older adults?
An 81-year-old woman with falls and mental clouding takes several medications, including amitriptyline. Which property of tricyclic antidepressants is relevant to medication review?

A 77-year-old man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22), depression, and mild cognitive impairment attends follow-up. His mood is stable, but he reports daytime fatigue and constipation. He takes sertraline 100 mg daily, sevelamer 800 mg three times daily with meals, and amitriptyline 25 mg at bedtime, recently added by his neurologist for insomnia. Laboratory results include potassium 5.2, BUN 78, creatinine 3.1, and hemoglobin 10.2. Which approach to amitriptyline is consistent with Beers 2023?
An older woman develops slowness and rigidity after starting a dopamine-blocking medication. Before adding Parkinson treatment, which medication-review step follows Hazzard?
Tramadol is being considered for an older patient who takes an antidepressant and has renal failure. Which pair of considerations matches Hazzard's medication table?

An 83-year-old woman in rehabilitation after a hip fracture cries, eats little, and says she wants to die. Her evaluation is not yet complete. What should be included immediately in suicide-risk assessment?
A 72-year-old man with severe depression has not improved after adequate medication trials. Electroconvulsive therapy is being considered. Which statement matches Hazzard’s explanation of treatment?
An older woman takes lithium, and addition of an ACE inhibitor is being considered. Which interaction and recommendation are described in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

An 82-year-old man with major depression, Parkinson disease, and mild cognitive impairment has not responded to several antidepressant trials. Pramipexole 0.5 mg three times daily is added to mirtazapine 30 mg nightly; he also takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg and entacapone 200 mg three times daily. Two days later, his wife reports new online gambling and inappropriate sexual comments. Which recognized dopamine-agonist adverse effect best matches these behaviors?

A 75-year-old woman with recurrent major depression and generalized anxiety has been stable on escitalopram 20 mg daily and buspirone 15 mg twice daily for two years. She develops dizziness, a fall, constipation, dry mouth, and mental slowing after nortriptyline 25 mg was added for nerve pain. Sodium is 128 mEq/L, potassium 3.8 mEq/L, and creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. Which action directly addresses the newly added strong anticholinergic exposure?

A person with dementia with Lewy bodies has recovered from a severe reaction to haloperidol. The patient is now stable but still has visual hallucinations and has not received cognitive treatment. Which drug trial is described by Hazzard as having the potential to reduce hallucinations in this condition?
A woman with fibromyalgia and depressive symptoms asks what duloxetine may contribute. Which combination of effects is described in Hazzard?

An 86-year-old resident with severe dementia newly resists care and reacts painfully to abdominal palpation. The cause has not been established. What is the appropriate approach before empirically changing analgesic treatment?
גבר בן 87 עם סרטן וכאב חמור מסרב למורפין בשל חשש מהתמכרות. לאחר הערכה נמצא שהוא מסוגל להבין את המידע ולקבל החלטה על הטיפול. אין מצב חירום. מה נדרש לפני החלטה טיפולית?

A 79-year-old woman with heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), mild cognitive impairment, and creatinine clearance 42 mL/min attends a palliative care clinic. She lives alone, recently began using a walker, and missed medication twice this week. She wants to maintain independence and avoid nursing home admission. Which advance care planning question identifies a surrogate decision maker?

An 84-year-old transgender woman with COPD, frailty (CFS 6), and depression is hospitalized with pneumonia. She transitioned three years ago and is estranged from her biological family. Her chosen family of LGBTQ friends visits, but hospital security questions their status as family. She withdraws from participation in care. Which response follows Hazzard's guidance on families of choice?

A 91-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, dysphagia and recurrent aspiration pneumonia is brought by his son for a goals-of-care discussion. He has lost 15 pounds in 3 months, sleeps 18 hours a day and needs full assistance with activities of daily living. His son insists on a PEG tube, saying, "I cannot let Dad starve." The patient previously expressed a wish to avoid tubes and machines. Which response best begins this conversation?
A 76-year-old woman with advanced cancer expresses fear of death and asks to talk about the future. How does Hazzard recommend opening the prognosis discussion?

An 81-year-old man with severe COPD (FEV1 28% predicted) has been hospitalized three times in six months, lost 20 pounds, and now needs help bathing and dressing. He asks how much time he has left. His daughter interrupts, saying everything will be fine. Which response follows the communication approach described in Hazzard?
מטופלת בישראל הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות ונמצאת במצב חירום רפואי. ידוע לצוות שרצונה להימנע מהטיפול המוצע במצב זה נקבע כדין לפי סעיף 5 לחוק החולה הנוטה למות. בתה מבקשת לבצעו. איזה עיקרון משפטי חל?

A 77-year-old Korean woman with pancreatic cancer is hospitalized for pain control. Through an interpreter she reports abdominal pain of 8/10. Her daughter asks you not to mention cancer, saying the family told her it was an infection and that this follows their cultural practice. The patient asks what is happening to her. Which approach follows the source guidance on disclosure?

An 83-year-old man with heart failure, stage 3b CKD (eGFR 35), and mild dementia is receiving hospice care for end-stage heart disease. Severe peripheral edema is causing skin breakdown and discomfort. He takes morphine 5 mg every four hours and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. His wife asks whether a diuretic could help. Which approach follows the source treatment of symptomatic congestion?
מטופלת עם דמנציה זקוקה לזמן ממושך ולעזרה באכילה. לאחר הערכת בליעה ותזונה נקבע שניתן לספק את צרכיה בבטחה דרך הפה, עם התאמות וסיוע. מהי הגישה המועדפת לפי המלצות הוועדה?

A 78-year-old man with metastatic cancer and uncontrolled pain says that he wants to die and that he has a gun. A suicidal plan and intent have not yet been assessed. Which action is needed now alongside treatment of his suffering?

An 82-year-old African American woman with ESRD on hemodialysis, severe peripheral arterial disease, and diabetes has right-foot gangrene. Vascular surgery recommends below-knee amputation. She refuses, saying she would rather die whole than live in pieces. Her son demands surgery, but psychiatric assessment confirms capacity for this decision. Which response respects her established decisional capacity?

A 79-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, legal blindness from macular degeneration, and a recent hip fracture is preparing for discharge from rehabilitation. She lives alone and wants to return home, despite two falls during rehabilitation and a physical therapist's finding that she needs supervision for safe walking. Her daughter requests nursing-home placement. MMSE is 27/30, with orientation and memory errors. What should guide assessment of her ability to decide about returning home?

An 86-year-old man with end-stage COPD, cor pulmonale, and a Clinical Frailty Scale score of 7 is admitted with hypercapnic respiratory failure. He is somnolent but arousable, with a PCO2 of 68. His POLST specifies do not intubate but not do not resuscitate. His wife requests BiPAP because it does not require intubation; the hospitalist believes it would prolong suffering. Which approach should guide the decision about respiratory support?
משפחת חולה עם דמנציה שהוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות מבקשת PEG. לפי המלצות הוועדה הארצית, מה צריך להנחות את הדיון בצורת ההזנה?
An 84-year-old man with knee osteoarthritis still has pain that limits walking despite topical and oral treatment. Which statement about a local intervention is supported by Hazzard?
A 79-year-old woman with an osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture asks when vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty is considered in Hazzard. Which situation supports considering it?

An 81-year-old man with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy has worsening burning foot pain for three months. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin; HbA1c is 8.2%, and monofilament sensation is absent bilaterally. He lives alone and recently stopped driving because of pain. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily caused severe dizziness. Which listed analgesic option belongs to the serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor class?

A 77-year-old woman with chronic low-back pain has marked lumbar facet arthropathy on MRI, local facet tenderness, and pain on extension and lateral rotation. She has hypertension and osteoporosis and takes amlodipine, alendronate, and acetaminophen. Physical therapy gave little relief, and tramadol caused nausea. Which description of medial branch blocks agrees with Hazzard?
A care-home resident with dementia and behavioral problems is assessed for possible pain. What was the first step in the empiric stepwise pain-treatment protocol described in Hazzard?
A 73-year-old man receiving an opioid for chronic pain develops somnolence and confusion. His renal function is impaired. Which mechanism explains increased susceptibility to adverse effects?

An 80-year-old woman with severe knee osteoarthritis has recurrent pain rated 7/10 that limits shopping. A course of three hyaluronic acid injections six months ago initially helped. She has heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35% and stage 3b CKD, and takes furosemide, lisinopril, and carvedilol. Examination shows an effusion and crepitus. She is reluctant to undergo the knee replacement recommended by her surgeon. Which injectable option has evidence for symptomatic relief in Hazzard, while the other choices are described as lacking clear benefit or remaining experimental?

A 78-year-old man has severe right-sided trigeminal neuralgia in the V2 distribution. He stopped gabapentin 300 mg three times daily because of delirium and has stopped shaving and eating solid food because of pain. He also has mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and glyburide. Which block does Hazzard specifically list for V2 trigeminal neuralgia?

An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?

A 75-year-old man with symptomatic lumbar spinal stenosis asks about epidural steroid injection. Which result matches the randomized trial in Hazzard comparing glucocorticoid plus lidocaine with lidocaine injection?

An 86-year-old woman has marked vulvovaginal discomfort during personal care. Examination shows severe atrophy, dryness, and fissures without infection or a suspicious lesion. She has no contraindication to local estrogen. Which treatment is preferred for the symptomatic atrophy?
An older woman who received an opioid for pain has tablets left after she no longer needs them. According to Hazzard, what should counseling about these tablets include?

An older woman with osteoporosis has sacral and buttock pain with local tenderness. Pelvic radiographs are negative, but suspicion of an insufficiency fracture remains high. Which principle follows Hazzard?

An older woman has persistent neuropathic facial pain and cannot tolerate anticonvulsant treatment because of sedation. After appropriate assessment, a nerve block is considered. Which role does Hazzard describe for the block?

An 81-year-old man has burning pain and allodynia in the left T10 dermatome six months after herpes zoster. Gabapentin and duloxetine have not helped. He has COPD, atrial fibrillation treated with apixaban, and stage 3 CKD; other medications are metoprolol, tiotropium, and acetaminophen. The pain prevents him from hugging his grandchildren. Which listed coanalgesic appears as a topical patch option in Hazzard’s Table 68-8?

An 84-year-old man with COPD is hospitalized for an exacerbation with acute hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis. He is alert, cooperative, stable, and able to protect his airway, with no contraindication to mask ventilation. Which approach is appropriate in addition to medical therapy?

A 78-year-old woman with moderate dementia (MMSE 18/30) has lost 8 kg in six months and now needs help bathing. She denies complaints. She takes donepezil 10 mg, metformin 500 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg. Albumin is 2.8, hemoglobin 10.2, and TSH is normal. Her daughter asks about appetite stimulants. After reversible causes have been addressed, which approach is supported without assuming proven benefit from an appetite stimulant?
An 81-year-old man with advanced illness wants relief of breathlessness while limiting medication burden. When should measures such as a fan and breathing techniques be introduced?
A 79-year-old woman with dementia is hospitalized with pneumonia and develops delirium. She is stable and is not endangering herself. Which environmental adjustment is appropriate?
גבר עם דמנציה מתקדמת נושא הנחיות מקדימות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות בנוגע להזנה מלאכותית. בטרם מפעילים אותן כמסלול ההחלטה, איזה מצב דורש סעיף 31?
A 77-year-old woman with recurrent falls takes amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. Which adverse-effect profile explains the concern about its use in older adults in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
An 82-year-old man with lung cancer appears independent and has good performance status. Why is comprehensive geriatric assessment still useful before chemotherapy?
An older woman with COPD and depression is being followed clinically. Which suicide-risk assessment is required as part of evaluating her depression?
בחולה עם דמנציה שהוגדר נוטה למות נשקלת דרך הזנה. מצבו מיוצב, והמשפחה מבקשת לדון באפשרויות. איזה עיקרון מנחה את קבלת ההחלטה לפי המלצות משרד הבריאות?
A 76-year-old man taking gabapentin for painful neuropathy has a creatinine clearance of 22 mL/min. Duloxetine is being considered. Which combination of decisions matches Table 6 of Beers 2023?

A stable woman is evaluated for suspected pulmonary embolism. Clinical probability is low, but the D-dimer result is positive. Renal function is normal and she has no contrast allergy. What is the appropriate next diagnostic step?
An older adult receiving chemotherapy for cancer has nausea. In addition to drug treatment, which dietary adjustment is described in Hazzard?

An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?

A 78-year-old man with COPD, coronary artery disease, and chronic pain from lumbar spinal stenosis has increasing dyspnea that limits him to climbing one flight of stairs. He takes formoterol/budesonide, tiotropium, aspirin, metoprolol, and oxycodone 5 mg four times daily. Spirometry is unchanged from baseline, with FEV1 35% predicted. His MRC dyspnea score is 3/5 and cardiac evaluation is negative. Which statement should guide referral for pulmonary rehabilitation?

An 83-year-old man with dementia develops delirium after starting quetiapine. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites, but there are no local urinary symptoms. He is stable and poses no danger to himself or staff. Which approach follows the source’s initial evaluation of delirium?

An 86-year-old man is readmitted with advanced lung disease. He is receiving treatment for an exacerbation but has severe symptoms and unclear goals of care. He is alert and wants to understand his options. When is palliative care consultation appropriate?

A 79-year-old woman with mild dementia develops an acute change in attention and awareness. She takes diphenhydramine and has hyponatremia. Urinalysis shows pyuria, but an infectious source has not been established. How should the evaluation proceed?

An 84-year-old man with frailty (four of five Fried criteria), heart failure, and moderate CKD (Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 35 mL/min) lives at home with a 24-hour caregiver. He has monthly heart-failure admissions despite optimized medication. A cardiologist recommends a primary-prevention ICD. The patient is hesitant, while his son, who holds medical power of attorney, strongly favors implantation. Before deciding about the device, which clinical approach best matches Hazzard?

אישה בישראל המטופלת בדיאליזה מחזורית הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. היא בעלת כשרות, מבינה את משמעות ההחלטה ומסרבת לחידוש הדיאליזה כדי שלא להאריך את חייה. מחזור הטיפול הקודם הסתיים. מהו העיקרון החל לפי החוק?

An 81-year-old man has fallen twice at night and reports insomnia. A falls assessment has been completed. He takes no sleep medication and has no sedative dependence. Which initial sleep approach is consistent with reducing exposure to medications implicated in falls?

אישה בת 92 עם דמנציה קשה (MMSE 8/30) בבית אבות לא אכלה במשך 5 ימים ואיבדה 15% ממשקל גופה במשך 3 חודשים. היא קופצת את פיה כאשר מציעים לה אוכל ודוחה כלי אוכל. הערכת בליעה אינה מראה ליקוי מכני. בתה מבקשת הכנסת צינור הזנה ואומרת: "אני לא יכולה לתת לאמי לגווע ברעב." כיצד צריך הצוות הפליאטיבי להגיב?
A 78-year-old man receiving morphine develops worsening renal function, somnolence, and myoclonus. Which medication-related mechanism should raise concern?
Intermittent catheterization is being considered for a woman with urinary retention. Which management principle follows Hazzard?

A 76-year-old man with COPD on home oxygen, heart failure (EF 25%), and stage 3b CKD has worsening dyspnea over several months despite optimized disease-directed treatment. He is homebound and uses a walker for short distances. His wife provides round-the-clock care and appears exhausted. He asks about hospice but says, “I am not ready to give up.” Which response best explains an available approach?
מטופל נקבע כחולה הנוטה למות ואינו בעל כשרות. נשקלות החלטות לפי החוק, ונמסר שבעבר הביע רצונות בנוגע לטיפול. מה נדרש מהרופא האחראי בבירור רצונו?

A 79-year-old woman with advanced heart failure asks about life expectancy so that she can plan. Her physician has a prognostic estimate but substantial uncertainty remains for the individual. How should it be communicated?

A patient near the end of life has severe agitated delirium. After an appropriate evaluation and initial treatment, sedation is agreed with the family to be consistent with the goals of care. Which drug characteristic is recommended?

An 85-year-old woman with severe COPD (FEV1 22%), osteoporosis, and severe frailty (CFS 7) lives alone with daily home help. She is hospitalized with influenza and respiratory failure requiring BiPAP. After recovery, she wants to return home and understands the risks, although the team is concerned about safety. Which plan combines her goal with the source approach to advanced COPD and diminished abilities?
גבר בן 77 לאחר ניתוח ודליריום שחלף משתתף בתכנון השיקום. הוא מבין את האפשרויות ואת השלכותיהן ומביע העדפה עקבית. מהו עיקרון שיתופו לפי חוזר משרד הבריאות על שיקום לקשישים?

An 80-year-old woman with advanced heart failure, moderate dementia, and pressure ulcers has lived in a nursing home for eight months. Monthly admissions for fluid overload are followed by functional decline. She cries during transfers and refuses physical therapy. Her son demands every treatment but has not visited for months. Which intervention directly addresses the need to clarify goals and align the care plan?

גבר בן 85 עם פרקינסון מתקדם בשלב 4 לפי H&Y ודמנציה מתונה מאושפז מבית אבות עם דלקת ריאות משאיפה. בתו, המחזיקה בייפוי כוח מתמשך, נפגשת איתך לדון במטרות הטיפול. היא אומרת: "הוא אמר לי שמעולם לא רצה להישאר בחיים על מכונות, אבל אני לא יכולה לתת לו למות. האם נוכל פשוט לנסות את המכונה כמה ימים?" התרופות הנוכחיות שלו כוללות carbidopa-levodopa, donepezil ו-quetiapine 50 mg QHS. סימנים חיוניים: T 38.5°C, HR 110, BP 95/60, RR 28, SpO2 88% על 6L O2. מהי התגובה הראשונית המתאימה ביותר?
A woman with advanced illness requests a survival estimate to plan her affairs. When a clinical estimate is available, how does Hazzard recommend communicating it?

An 81-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 18) presents after a fall. His daughter reports more confusion and frequent falls. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, and trazodone 100 mg nightly, started two weeks ago for sleep. Blood pressure is 140/80 supine and 110/65 standing. Which action directly removes the newly introduced drug associated in Hazzard with daytime sleepiness and orthostatic hypotension?
בת 92 עם דמנציה מתקדמת הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. משפחתה מבקשת PEG בגלל שאיפות חוזרות. מה מתואר בסיכום המחקרים במסמך הוועדה הארצית, לצד ההסתייגות ממגבלותיהם?

An 84-year-old man with heart failure and impaired renal function takes spironolactone. Creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL and potassium 5.3 mEq/L. Which adjustment matches the contraindications in Hazzard's heart-failure chapter?

A 79-year-old woman with dementia becomes acutely confused after starting oxybutynin. She is stable, with no fever, dysuria, flank pain, or new urinary symptom. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites. She has no catheter, focal neurologic deficit, or immediately dangerous behavior. Which approach is appropriate now?

מטופל מבוגר המסוגל לקבל החלטות מבקש להשוות בין החייאה עתידית לבין חלופותיה. כבר הוסברו לו האבחנה, הפרוגנוזה ומהות פעולות ההחייאה. איזה מידע נוסף נותן מענה לחובת ההסבר על הטיפול ועל החלופות לפי סעיף 13(ב) לחוק זכויות החולה?
אישה בת 77 עם סרטן ודליריום נבדקה בזמן צלילות ונמצאה מסוגלת לקבל את ההחלטה הטיפולית הנדונה. אין מצב חירום. ילדיה חלוקים לגבי הטיפול, והיא מבקשת הסבר כדי להחליט. מה צריך להנחות את השיחה?
An 82-year-old man with falls has taken lorazepam every night for two years. Which consideration supports reviewing the treatment with attention to physical dependence, according to Beers 2023?
A woman with COPD remains breathless at rest despite optimal treatment of her lung disease. Which principle applies to drug treatment of refractory dyspnea according to Hazzard?
A woman with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction has pulmonary congestion and is receiving a diuretic. Which principle should guide adjustment of treatment intensity?

A 91-year-old man with Parkinson disease, falls, and orthostatic hypotension takes amitriptyline for pain. The team has decided to remove an antidepressant with strong anticholinergic activity. Which plan accomplishes this under Beers 2023?
אישה עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה יכולה להבין ולקבל החלטות בנוגע לענייניה כאשר המידע מונגש לה. נשקלת קבלת החלטות נתמכת בישראל. מהו תפקיד התומך?
An 83-year-old man with metastatic cancer and uncontrolled pain says he will harm himself if the pain continues. In addition to treating pain, what should be assessed now to evaluate suicide risk?

An 80-year-old woman with heart failure, chronic kidney disease and newly diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. The oncologist recommends pembrolizumab, while the cardiologist is concerned about cardiac toxicity. She lives independently and manages her instrumental activities. She says, "I want to fight the cancer, but I also want to be at home with my grandchildren." What should the team clarify to align the treatment plan with her priorities?

An 85-year-old man with mild dementia (MMSE 22), hypertension, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45) has developed increasing difficulty managing finances, finding his way to familiar places, and taking medications over three weeks. His wife died six months ago. His daughter asks about supported accommodation, but he wants to remain at home. Examination and routine laboratory results are normal. Alongside evaluation of this recent change, which approach directly assesses whether his home setting can meet his current needs?
למטופלת בעלת יכולת לקבל החלטות מוצע טיפול נשימתי ב-BiPAP. היא חוששת מהמשמעות של טיפול זה. איזה מידע יש למסור לצורך הסכמה מדעת לפי סעיף 13 לחוק זכויות החולה?

An 81-year-old man with diabetes fell during documented hypoglycemia. His oral glucose-lowering therapy is being reviewed to reduce further episodes. Which listed drug belongs to a class with a significant risk of hypoglycemia?
מטופלת עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה מתקשה לעקוב אחר הסבר על ניתוח מתוכנן. בנה מבקש מהרופא להחליט במקומה. מהו עיקרון ההסבר לצורך הסכמה מדעת לפי חוק זכויות החולה?
בישראל, הובאו לרופא הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות שתוקפן פג, עבור חולה הנוטה למות שאינו יכול להביע את רצונו. כיצד מתייחס אליהן החוק?

A 78-year-old woman with diabetes and mild dementia lives alone. Her A1C is 9.2% on metformin; she forgets medications and meals. Her daughter requests insulin, but the patient does not want injections. Her MMSE is 28/30, although medication tasks require prompting. After reviewing her goals and arranging adherence support, an oral DPP-4 inhibitor is being discussed. Which description of this drug class matches Hazzard?

An 86-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis, stage 3b CKD, and frailty (CFS 6) is offered TAVR. He uses a wheelchair, needs help with all IADLs, and receives continuous care from his wife. He wants comfort and to die at home when the time comes. His cardiologist emphasizes possible life prolongation; his wife is uncertain. What should the team do next?

אישה בת 83 עם פרקינסון מתקדם ודיספגיה מאושפזת עקב דלקת ריאות אספירטיבית. קלינאית תקשורת ממליצה על NPO עם צינור הזנה. לה יש מצב קוגניטיבי משתנה, אך בתקופות צלולות היא אומרת: 'עדיף לי למות מאשר לקבל צינור הזנה - ראיתי את אמי סובלת עם אחד כזה.' בתה מתעקשת: 'היא פשוט מבולבלת - היא צריכה תזונה.' לחולה אין הנחיות מקדימות. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?
בן 80 עם סרטן לבלב גרורתי שוקל ERCP להקלה על חסימה. הוא מסוגל להחליט ואומר שברצונו לבלות זמן עם נכדיו; אשתו מדגישה הימנעות מאשפוז. לפני המלצה משותפת, איזה צעד שומר על בחירה מדעת של המטופל?

A 76-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer disease has recurrent urinary tract infections associated with delirium. Between infections she lives with family, recognizes loved ones, and enjoys daily activities. Urologic evaluation found no anatomical abnormality. She cannot express treatment preferences, and her daughter asks about preventive antibiotics. Which process follows shared decision-making?

גבר בן 82 מאושפז עם קוליטיס על רקע C. difficile חמורה, הישנות שלישית למרות vancomycin פומי. גסטרואנטרולוגיה ממליצה על השתלת צואה (FMT). יש לו ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה (MCI) אך הוא מבין את הפרוצדורה. הוא אומר: 'זה מגעיל — לעולם לא אעשה את זה.' בנו טוען: 'הוא סתם עקשן — הוא ימות בלי זה. אי אפשר פשוט לעשות את זה?' למטופל יש כשירות. מה התגובה המתאימה?

A 79-year-old woman with COPD, heart failure, and diabetes develops acute kidney injury during a heart-failure exacerbation. Dialysis is recommended. Her POLST specifies limited interventions, and she says she does not want dialysis after seeing her husband’s experience. The team confirms that she understands the relevant risks, benefits, and alternatives and has capacity for this decision. Her daughter asks the team to proceed because she believes her mother is frightened. Which action follows the principle described in Hazzard?
חולה נוטה למות אינו בעל כשרות ובני משפחתו חלוקים לגבי רצונו. במסגרת הבירור לפי סעיף 9 נמצאו במאגר הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות. כיצד יש לטפל במידע שנמצא?
בישראל, חולה הנוטה למות מפתחת דליריום. הצוות שוקל לקבוע שאינה כשירה להחליט על הטיפול לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות. מה נדרש להוצאתה מחזקת הכשירות?

גבר בן 81 עם דמנציה קלה והיסטוריה קרדיאלית נרחבת מאושפז עם NSTEMI. הקרדיולוגיה ממליצה על קתטריזציה. במהלך תהליך ה-consent, הוא שואל שוב ושוב 'האם זה יתקן את בעיות הזיכרון שלי?' למרות הסברים חוזרים, הוא מתקבע על שיפור קוגניטיבי. בתו אומרת: 'יש לו capacity להחלטות אחרות – אנא המשיכו.' כיצד על הרופא לגשת ל-consent?
An older patient with HFpEF and hypertension presents for treatment planning. Which basic principle does Hazzard emphasize?

A 79-year-old woman has recurrent near-syncope when rising from a chair after recently starting doxazosin 4 mg nightly for hypertension. Blood pressure is 158/78 supine and 122/68 after three minutes standing, with pulse rising from 68 to 74. Her daughter reports two falls this month and refusal to shower alone. She also takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Which medication-review approach follows the Beers recommendation for doxazosin used as an antihypertensive?

An 86-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 19) and peripheral arterial disease has stable exertional chest pressure during daily walks. Angiography shows an 80% LAD stenosis; EF is 52% and eGFR 48. His wife reports missed medication doses and a recent episode of getting lost near home. He has not yet had a trial of optimized antianginal treatment. Which initial strategy matches Hazzard's approach to stable ischemic heart disease?

A 77-year-old woman takes diphenhydramine every night for sleep and presents with confusion and falls. During review using Beers 2023, which change addresses the anticholinergic burden suspected of contributing to her symptoms?
