A patient with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is eligible to switch from an ACE inhibitor to sacubitril/valsartan. Why is a washout period required between the treatments?

An 83-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation takes warfarin. After a fall, her INR is 3.8 and head CT is normal. She reports dietary difficulties and frequent INR fluctuations. Her CHA2DS2-VASc score is 5, HAS-BLED score 3, weight 58 kg, and serum creatinine 1.3 mg/dL. If apixaban is selected, how should the dose-reduction criteria in Hazzard be applied?

An older patient develops delirium after admission for myocardial infarction and coronary catheterization. Several medications were started together. Which approach to evaluating medication contributions follows Hazzard?

An 85-year-old woman with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, mild dementia, and frailty lives alone with daily aide support. Her daughter asks about transcatheter and surgical valve replacement. Which comparative statement agrees with Hazzard?
An older woman is starting a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. Which pair of measurements is particularly important during initiation and dose titration?

An 82-year-old man taking rivaroxaban develops severe bleeding. Alongside stabilization and assessment of the bleeding source, which agent does Hazzard describe as a decoy protein that binds and sequesters factor Xa inhibitors?

A 79-year-old woman with new atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc score 4) and stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 38) starts amiodarone for rhythm control after unsuccessful metoprolol and diltiazem treatment. Baseline QTc is 438 ms. Two weeks later, she develops tremor and heat intolerance. TSH is 0.02, previously 2.1, and free T4 is 3.8 (reference range 0.8–1.8). Which approach best reflects Hazzard's management of amiodarone-associated thyroid dysfunction?
An 84-year-old man is being assessed for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. Which principle does Hazzard describe for decision-making in very old patients?
An older woman with unilateral renal artery stenosis and stable kidney function asks about a stent. Which statement agrees with the discussion of stable renal artery disease in Hazzard?
An 81-year-old ambulatory woman has uncontrolled hypertension and needs a treatment adjustment. Which principle should guide initiation and dose titration in older adults according to Hazzard?
After TAVR, several patients develop conduction abnormalities. Which finding is an indication for permanent pacemaker implantation before discharge in Hazzard?
Prasugrel is being considered for an 84-year-old patient after percutaneous coronary intervention. What is the reason for the age-related warning described by Hazzard?

A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis has fallen twice in the past month. She describes the episodes as tripping. Medications are amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, and ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily. Blood pressure is 138/82 seated and 116/70 after three minutes standing. Creatinine is 1.4 mg/dL compared with a baseline of 1.0. Which principle from Hazzard addresses potentially medication-related orthostatic hypotension?

An 81-year-old man with stable coronary disease, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) had his last myocardial infarction three years ago. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. LDL is 72 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.8%. His wife reports missed evening doses. Which prescribing approach directly addresses the regimen-complexity problem described by Hazzard?
A 77-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation and an eGFR of 52 takes apixaban. What additional information is needed to assess the dose-reduction criteria in Hazzard Table 77-9?

An 85-year-old man without known cardiovascular disease, with mild cognitive decline and falls, is referred for consideration of a statin for primary prevention. Which approach is consistent with Hazzard?
An older woman with acute coronary syndrome and renal impairment is being considered for low-molecular-weight heparin. Which consideration should guide treatment adjustment?

An 82-year-old man with coronary disease, previous bypass surgery, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease is euvolemic after treatment of decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. He takes carvedilol, lisinopril, and furosemide. Spironolactone is being considered. Which statement follows Hazzard's description of this treatment?
An older woman taking a statin develops muscle pain and a CK level 12 times the upper limit of normal. Which action regarding the statin is supported by Hazzard?

An 80-year-old man with a myocardial infarction 12 years ago, chronic stable angina, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease attends a medication review. He functions well and walks two miles daily without symptoms. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg, and atorvastatin 40 mg. Blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg, heart rate is 64 beats/min, and a recent echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 55%. Before deciding whether to deprescribe metoprolol, which finding would support deprescribing under Hazzard's framework?

A nursing-home resident takes aspirin and clopidogrel, but their original indication is unclear in the record. She has developed extensive bruising. What belongs in the prescription review before deciding whether to continue treatment?

A 77-year-old woman without known atherosclerotic disease is being assessed before a decision about statin therapy for primary prevention. She has mild cognitive decline. Which approach reflects the uncertainty described in Hazzard?
An 86-year-old man with atrial fibrillation and a previous bleed is being assessed before antithrombotic treatment. Which pairing matches the purposes of the two risk tools described in Hazzard?
An older woman with stable angina is taking a beta blocker. Which mechanism describes its anti-ischemic action according to Hazzard?

An 81-year-old man with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation is selected for apixaban. He weighs 75 kg and his serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. There is no other indication for dose adjustment. How should the dose-reduction criteria in the Hazzard table be applied?
A 79-year-old woman has had a myocardial infarction and can tolerate statin therapy. Which goal of intensive lipid-lowering therapy in this period is supported by Hazzard?

An 84-year-old man with HFrEF, ejection fraction 35%, stage 4 CKD with eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m2, and mild cognitive impairment has worsening breathlessness and 3+ pitting edema despite prescribed furosemide 40 mg twice daily. Blood pressure is 108/68, heart rate 72, creatinine 2.8 mg/dL from a baseline of 2.2, potassium 4.8, and BNP 1850. His daughter reports missed medication doses and daily canned soup. Alongside assessment and treatment of congestion, which action directly addresses the adherence problem?

A 79-year-old woman with HFpEF (EF 58%), type 2 diabetes, and frailty is recovering after diuresis for decompensated heart failure. When considering empagliflozin, which result of EMPEROR-Preserved reported in Hazzard is relevant?
An 81-year-old woman with diabetes receives insulin and a beta-blocker for cardiovascular disease. Which beta-blocker effect is relevant to hypoglycemia safety?

A patient with HFpEF receives diuretics for congestion. Excessive diuresis is followed by fatigue, lower blood pressure, and prerenal azotemia. Which hemodynamic change explains this volume sensitivity?

An 85-year-old woman with HFrEF (EF 28%), moderate Alzheimer dementia, and creatinine clearance of 32 mL/min has improved after intravenous furosemide for fluid overload. Her regular medications are lisinopril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily, and furosemide 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 102/58 mm Hg. Her family asks about sacubitril/valsartan. The team is assessing tolerability and whether to switch. If an ACE-inhibitor-to-ARNI switch is selected, which initiation plan follows Hazzard?

A 78-year-old man with HFrEF, an ejection fraction of 25%, and NYHA class III symptoms despite optimally tolerated treatment is in sinus rhythm with LBBB and a QRS duration of 160 milliseconds. Following a goals-of-care discussion, which intervention targets synchronized ventricular contraction?

An 82-year-old woman taking a diuretic has volume depletion and a total-body sodium deficit. There is no suspicion of combined poisoning or adrenal insufficiency. Which treatment principle is consistent with Hazzard?

A 79-year-old man with advanced heart failure and additional comorbidities is referred for evaluation for a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). He is unsure whether it fits his goals. When does Hazzard recommend incorporating palliative care consultation?
בישראל, חולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות סובל סבל משמעותי, ורצונו להימנע מהארכת חיים נקבע כדין. הוא אינו בשלב סופי. לפי סעיף 16 לחוק, מה דינו של טיפול נלווה שאינו קשור למחלה חשוכת המרפא?

A 76-year-old woman with newly diagnosed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction feels less breathless after starting low-dose lisinopril. Follow-up shows a small rise in creatinine and potassium, without symptomatic hypotension. The clinician is reviewing whether to continue treatment. Which principle is consistent with Hazzard?
מטופל עם אי ספיקת לב קשה התייצב לאחר טיפול דחוף. כעת הוא מסוגל להבין ולקבל החלטות, ונשקל טיפול נוסף שאינו דחוף. מהי הדרך המתאימה לקבל הסכמה מדעת לפי חוק זכויות החולה?

A 77-year-old woman with HFpEF (EF 58%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and biopsy-proven transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis has NYHA class II symptoms despite furosemide 40 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Echocardiography shows LV wall thickening and grade 2 diastolic dysfunction. Which treatment is the TTR stabilizer described in Hazzard as reducing mortality versus placebo in ATTR-ACT?

An 81-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, mild Alzheimer disease, and recurrent falls is receiving guideline-directed treatment and has a CRT-D. He now spends more time in bed, eats less, appears sad, has lost weight, and shows muscle wasting, weak grip, and slow gait. Which assessment addresses physical, functional, psychological, and socioenvironmental needs together?

An 86-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis is not a candidate for valve replacement. The heart team discusses balloon aortic valvuloplasty as a palliative option. What role does Hazzard describe for this procedure?
A 78-year-old man with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction takes a low-dose ACE inhibitor. He is to switch to sacubitril/valsartan. Which approach is consistent with Hazzard?
Ventricular rate-control treatment is being considered for an older man with atrial fibrillation. Which consideration in choosing treatment is supported by Hazzard?

A 79-year-old woman takes digoxin. After her renal function worsens, she develops nausea, confusion, and a conduction abnormality. Urgent evaluation has begun, and her serum digoxin concentration is within the laboratory's therapeutic range. How should this result be interpreted?

An 88-year-old man with dementia and aortic stenosis is being evaluated in the United States for Medicare hospice care. Beyond diagnoses and residence, which information is required to establish eligibility?

A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and newly diagnosed paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is being assessed for anticoagulation. Her creatinine clearance is in the 30–49 mL/min range. She takes metformin, glipizide, amlodipine, and metoprolol, lives alone, manages daily tasks independently, and sometimes forgets medication doses. If rivaroxaban is selected, which statement agrees with Hazzard's table?

An 81-year-old man with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is being considered for an ICD. He recently fell and needs help managing his affairs. Which consideration accurately describes the discussion of implantation in Hazzard?

A 76-year-old woman takes gabapentin for pain and has a creatinine clearance of 40 mL/min. According to the Beers 2023 renal table, what change addresses the risk of central nervous system adverse effects?
An 85-year-old man with atrial fibrillation and unstable renal function needs ventricular rate control. How does Hazzard characterize digoxin relative to first-line agents?

An older woman with atrial fibrillation, mild symptoms, and stable heart failure with an EF of 35% needs initial ventricular rate-control therapy. Renal function is unstable. Which initial drug approach matches Hazzard?
A 78-year-old man with typical atrial flutter is being considered for catheter ablation. Which structure is the critical conduction pathway in the typical flutter circuit described by Hazzard?

An 82-year-old woman with heart failure (EF 35%), permanent atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes is admitted with volume overload. She functions independently, but her daughter reports recent difficulty managing medications. Her medications are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, furosemide 80 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, apixaban 5 mg twice daily, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.3), and BNP 1850. ECG shows atrial fibrillation at 78 beats/min with QRS 118 ms. Which approach to spironolactone follows Hazzard's safety guidance?
חולה עם ICD מבקש שינוי בטיפול בסוף החיים. לפני החלת חוק החולה הנוטה למות, מי מוסמך לקבוע שהמטופל הוא חולה הנוטה למות לפי החוק?
An 86-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation and mild symptoms asks about rate control versus rhythm control. Which conclusion reflects Hazzard?

A 75-year-old man survives a witnessed ventricular-fibrillation arrest at his gym. CPR begins immediately and circulation returns after two shocks. He has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Angiography shows 40% mid-LAD stenosis without intervention; echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 42% without regional wall-motion abnormalities. He is extubated on day 3 and is neurologically intact. Evaluation identifies no transient or reversible cause. Which conclusion about ICD therapy follows from Hazzard?
An 83-year-old woman taking digoxin and furosemide develops hypokalemia and new arrhythmias. Which relationship between these findings is important to recognize?

A 77-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, and a left ventricular ejection fraction below 40% has recurrent activity-limiting episodes despite high-dose metoprolol. Between episodes his heart rate and blood pressure are low. He receives anticoagulation. Which next strategy best fits the source?

An 84-year-old man with symptomatic carotid stenosis is being assessed for intervention. Which comparison between carotid endarterectomy and transfemoral carotid artery stenting is described by Hazzard?
A 78-year-old woman is under surveillance for an asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm. According to Hazzard, which finding is the main determinant of rupture risk and the timing of intervention?

An 81-year-old man with a 4.8-cm abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoes annual ultrasound surveillance. Which recommendation agrees with Hazzard’s surveillance and medical-management principles for a small aneurysm?

A 79-year-old woman has peripheral arterial disease (ABI 0.45), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22), and a recent fall with hip fracture. Claudication now limits walking to 50 feet, and duplex shows 80% superficial femoral artery stenosis. She takes clopidogrel 75 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. When planning exercise within her safe capabilities, which walking approach is described for claudication?

An 86-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate vascular dementia, hypertension, and a 4.2-cm abdominal aortic aneurysm stable for two years requires help with all activities of daily living; BIMS is 8/15. During a goals-of-care meeting, the team confirms his previously expressed preference for comfort-focused care. After an individualized discussion, aneurysm repair would not be pursued and surveillance results would not change his care. Which approach applies Hazzard’s goals-based principle?

An older man with postoperative delirium endangers himself and interrupts essential care despite nonpharmacologic measures. A short antipsychotic trial is being considered. What is its intended role in this setting?
An 82-year-old woman undergoing preoperative evaluation has an elevated Clinical Frailty Scale score. How should this information be used?
A 75-year-old man taking clopidogrel before surgery asks why it belongs in the bleeding-risk assessment. Which explanation is consistent with Hazzard?

An 80-year-old woman with peripheral arterial disease and intermittent claudication remains limited in walking despite supervised exercise. She takes an antiplatelet agent and a statin, has no heart failure, and is not currently scheduled for a vascular intervention. Which additional recommendation is supported by Hazzard?

An 83-year-old man is being evaluated for a suspected prosthetic device infection. He is clinically stable, has no sepsis, and cultures can safely be obtained. According to Hazzard, what should guide antibiotic treatment?
A 76-year-old woman treated for hypertension reports dizziness on standing. Which measurement principle is important before changing treatment?

An 85-year-old man is under surveillance for an asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm. According to Hazzard, which anatomical measurement is the major determinant of rupture risk and the timing of intervention?

A 78-year-old woman develops acute confusion, visual hallucinations, and nighttime agitation after femoral endarterectomy. The CAM is positive and there are no focal neurologic findings. She takes gabapentin 300 mg three times daily for neuropathic pain. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL, previously 1.2; sodium is 138 mmol/L and glucose 95 mg/dL. Which medication-review approach is appropriate while the team investigates delirium?

An 81-year-old man with carotid stenosis and significant heart disease is being assessed for intervention. Which consideration explains why transfemoral carotid stenting does not simply remove the procedural risks in this age group?

A 79-year-old woman with peripheral arterial disease reports new rest pain after bypass surgery. Before attributing it to neuropathic pain and choosing an analgesic, which vascular mechanism should be assessed?
A 78-year-old man with diabetes and chronic kidney disease is having his hypertension treatment reviewed. How should the treatment goal be set according to Hazzard?

An 84-year-old woman taking hydrochlorothiazide develops postural dizziness and weight loss after poor intake. Clinical assessment confirms volume depletion. There is no congestion or evidence of adrenal disease. Which approach is appropriate?
A 79-year-old man with heart failure has pulmonary congestion and edema. A loop diuretic is being considered. What is the principal expected benefit described by Hazzard?

An 81-year-old woman attends a routine visit without acute symptoms or evidence of acute target-organ injury. A single blood pressure measurement after walking to the clinic is higher than usual. What should be done before diagnosing sustained hypertension and changing treatment?
An older man with hypertension and a previous myocardial infarction is being considered for a beta-blocker. Which consideration supports its use according to Hazzard?

An 85-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease, dysphagia, recurrent aspiration pneumonia, and complete dependence for daily activities has persistently elevated blood pressure. His representative asks about treatment. Before selecting a drug, which approach follows Hazzard for a person with high comorbidity burden and limited life expectancy?

A 76-year-old woman with hypertension and mild frailty walks with a walker and covers 5.2 meters in 8 seconds. Her baseline blood pressure is 148/82 on amlodipine 5 mg daily. In a trial she is assigned to an intensive systolic blood pressure target below 120 mm Hg. After amlodipine titration and addition of lisinopril, her blood pressure is 118/68 seated and 114/66 standing. She feels well and reports more energy. Which interpretation of the SPRINT evidence supports continuing her tolerated regimen with monitoring?
Chlorthalidone is being considered for hypertension in an older patient. How does Hazzard describe it in comparison with hydrochlorothiazide?
A 73-year-old woman with hypertension takes a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug for joint pain. What is the role of reviewing this medication in her blood pressure evaluation?

A 78-year-old man has recovered from pneumonia. Repeated clinic and home blood pressure readings are around 170/90 mm Hg, without orthostatic hypotension. He has untreated stage 2 hypertension and no coronary disease or heart failure. Combination treatment is planned. Which initial regimen best fits the Hazzard approach?

An 82-year-old woman with dementia sometimes refuses tablets. After the team adjusts medication administration, she willingly accepts oral treatment. Persistent hypertension requires treatment; a thiazide previously caused hyponatremia, and there is no cardiac indication for a beta-blocker. Renal function and potassium are normal. Which class is the most appropriate initial choice among these options according to Hazzard?

A 75-year-old man with hypertension, prediabetes, and BPH takes chlorthalidone 25 mg daily and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. His blood pressure is 146/84. He reports dizziness on standing quickly and nocturia four to five times nightly that disrupts sleep. Glucose is 118, potassium 3.4, and creatinine 1.1. When reviewing possible thiazide adverse effects, which strategy follows the principles described in Hazzard?

A 77-year-old woman presents after a fall and reports a month of dizziness on standing. She takes amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, and lisinopril 20 mg each morning. Blood pressure is 138/78 supine and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 68 to 74. Potassium is 3.3 and creatinine 1.2. During medication review, which option both removes the thiazide exposure associated with potassium loss and provides potassium replacement?

An 81-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment has increasing confusion over two weeks. His family reports good medication adherence. He takes metformin, amlodipine, losartan, and recently added trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection, now on day five of seven. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.3), glucose 142, and blood pressure 128/76. Which medication-review plan best addresses the drug interaction relevant to his laboratory findings?

A 79-year-old woman with hypertension has maintained blood pressure below her individual target on stable treatment after successful lifestyle changes. Which approach to reducing treatment does Hazzard describe?

A 78-year-old man with severe COPD (FEV1 35% predicted) presents with acute dyspnea and confusion. His daughter reports two days of memory difficulty and failure to recognize her this morning. His home medications include tiotropium, budesonide/formoterol, and lorazepam 0.5 mg three times daily, recently started for anxiety. Arterial blood gases show pH 7.32, pCO2 58, and pO2 65 on 2 L/min by nasal cannula. Chest radiography shows hyperinflation without infiltrates, and examination reveals asterixis. Medication review focuses on a possible benzodiazepine contribution. Which effect described by Hazzard is relevant?

A patient with delirium is found to be volume depleted while taking furosemide. There is no congestion, and the team identifies overdiuresis as a contributor. Which approach addresses the identified problem?
A 75-year-old man with COPD remains limited when walking by dyspnea and fatigue despite optimized pharmacologic therapy. How should pulmonary rehabilitation be approached?

An 84-year-old nursing-home resident with severe COPD, moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 18), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) presents with acute dyspnea. He is uncomfortable but follows simple commands. His MOLST specifies no intubation but permits bilevel positive airway pressure. Arterial blood gases show pH 7.28, PaCO2 68 mm Hg, and PaO2 58 mm Hg; chest radiography shows no infiltrate. His son asks about comfort-focused care. Which initial ventilatory approach is supported by the source and the stated treatment preferences?

A woman with COPD uses albuterol frequently and remains symptomatic. After evaluation of the poor symptom control, a long-acting bronchodilator is being considered. How does Hazzard's drug table distinguish SABA from LABA therapy?

An 81-year-old man with severe COPD on continuous oxygen at 2 L/min and mild cognitive impairment develops worsening confusion over three days, poor sleep, and hallucinations. He recently finished antibiotics for an exacerbation. He takes tiotropium, budesonide/formoterol, a prednisone taper currently at 20 mg, and temazepam 15 mg nightly, started one week ago. Which action addresses the newly introduced benzodiazepine exposure during the delirium evaluation?

A 76-year-old woman with COPD has an FEV1 of 45% predicted, sarcopenia with a grip strength of 14 kg, and increasing difficulty bathing independently despite optimized bronchodilator therapy. She has lost 8 lb over 6 months; BMI is 19.2 and albumin is 3.1 g/dL. She asks about prognosis and hospice. Which assessment combines nutritional status, airflow obstruction, dyspnea, and exercise capacity to inform the prognosis discussion?

An 85-year-old man with COPD and chronic kidney disease is hospitalized with pneumonia. He develops delirium with agitation that threatens essential treatment despite nonpharmacologic measures. After assessing risks, the team decides to use haloperidol. Which initial approach matches Hazzard?

A 77-year-old woman with moderate COPD and frailty has lost 15 lb unintentionally, reports exhaustion, and has a grip strength of 15 kg. She has temporal wasting and reduced breath sounds, uses tiotropium and as-needed albuterol, and has had progressive breathlessness for two weeks. She is unable to climb to her bedroom and sleeps in a recliner; her daughter is considering nursing-home placement. After evaluation of her recent deterioration and stabilization of her respiratory illness, which rehabilitation plan directly addresses exercise limitation and nutritional needs?
A patient with COPD develops respiratory depression after an opioid overdose. Alongside respiratory support, treatment is needed to reverse the opioid effect. What is the role of naloxone here?
במשפחתו של מטופל עם דמנציה נשקל מעבר מהזנה בזונדה להזנה דרך PEG. מה יש להסביר על ההשוואה בין שתי דרכי ההזנה לפי המלצות הוועדה הארצית?
At discharge, a patient with COPD reports being unable to keep taking inhalers because of their cost. What should the adherence assessment include, according to Hazzard?
An older woman with atrial fibrillation develops a slower heart rate after rapid beta-blocker dose escalation. Which drug effect explains why its contribution should be considered?
חולה בישראל הוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות וסובל מקוצר נשימה קשה. הוא מבקש הקלה בסבלו. איזה עיקרון תואם את סעיף 23 לחוק החולה הנוטה למות?

An 84-year-old man is hospitalized with a COPD exacerbation, acute hypercarbia, and respiratory acidosis. He is conscious, cooperative, able to protect his airway, and hemodynamically stable. There is no contraindication to a face mask. What is the role of noninvasive positive pressure ventilation in this setting?

A 79-year-old woman with COPD, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment lives alone. She uses her albuterol inhaler “when I remember” and reports difficulty with inhaler technique. Her daughter finds expired inhalers and reports two hospitalizations for exacerbations in six months. FEV1 is 48% predicted. Her medications are as-needed albuterol MDI, daily tiotropium HandiHaler, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Which intervention addresses her difficulty delivering inhaled bronchodilators?

An 81-year-old nursing-home resident with severe COPD, dementia, and recurrent aspiration becomes poorly responsive after starting oral morphine for dyspnea. He has marked respiratory slowing, hypoxemia, and hypercapnic respiratory acidosis. His directive requests DNR status but continuation of medical treatment. Which approach addresses a reversible drug effect while recognizing the severely impaired consciousness?

A 77-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 55%), hypertension, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m2) is reviewed after an exacerbation treated with prednisone 40 mg for 5 days. He remains breathless when dressing and can no longer shop independently. He takes tiotropium, as-needed albuterol, amlodipine 10 mg, and lisinopril 20 mg. Blood pressure is 128/76 and room-air oxygen saturation is 93%. Alongside review of his drug treatment, which pulmonary rehabilitation approach is supported by Hazzard?
A hospitalized woman develops delirium after a medication change. Evaluation identifies a drug that could be contributing to confusion. Which approach addresses the medication-related cause?

A 75-year-old man with stable COPD receives optimal inhaled treatment. Two resting room-air measurements show PaO2 58 mm Hg; PaCO2 is 52 mm Hg and pH is normal. He has cor pulmonale with edema and no recent exacerbation. Which recommendation follows the long-term oxygen indications and survival evidence in Hazzard?
A woman with COPD remains limited by dyspnea despite optimized pharmacologic therapy. Which nonpharmacologic intervention is appropriate now according to the COPD chapter?
חולה בישראל הוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות. אשתו וילדיו חלוקים לגבי רצונותיו הקודמים, וטרם נאספו נתונים ומסמכים רלוונטיים. מהי חובת הרופא בשלב בירור הרצון?
An older adult has suspected opioid overdose with respiratory depression. Naloxone is considered during emergency treatment. What is its purpose?

A 76-year-old man with persistent pain and kidney impairment is being considered for opioid treatment after assessment of benefits and risks. Which initiation and follow-up strategy is described in Hazzard?

בת 83 עם דמנציה מתקדמת הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. יש קושי בבליעה, אך הערכה רב־מקצועית קבעה שניתן לספק את צורכי המזון והנוזלים דרך הפה בעזרת התאמות וסיוע. לפי המלצות המותב הארצי, איזו דרך הזנה מועדפת במצב זה?

A 77-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 45%), coronary disease, and diabetes has had four admissions for COPD exacerbations in eight months. Between admissions he needs help with basic ADLs from his older wife, who is exhausted. Creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min by Cockcroft–Gault. He takes 14 medications, including warfarin requiring frequent INR testing, and says, “I am tired of the struggle.” Which referral plan explicitly integrates symptom management, discussion of care goals, and support for the family?
A patient with COPD uses albuterol frequently. Which pair of adverse effects of short-acting beta-2 agonists is listed in Hazzard?

A 79-year-old woman with COPD and osteoporosis needs systemic corticosteroids for a moderate to severe exacerbation. How should exposure-related harm be limited while preserving beneficial treatment, according to Hazzard?

An 81-year-old man with advanced COPD has refractory dyspnea despite optimal treatment of the underlying disease. An opioid is being considered for palliation. Which potential benefit and cognitive risk are described by Hazzard?
An older patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease takes metformin and has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 32 mL/min/1.73 m². Which monitoring principle is consistent with Hazzard?
An older woman with advanced kidney disease develops unexplained behavioral changes and cognitive impairment. What possibility should be considered according to Hazzard?
A patient with chronic kidney disease requests treatment for joint pain. Which prescribing principle is emphasized in Hazzard’s chapter on the aging kidney?
An older woman with reduced renal clearance is taking a medication excreted by the kidney. Which principle should guide a safety review of the prescription?

A 77-year-old man with atrial fibrillation and moderate mitral stenosis needs anticoagulation for stroke prevention. Which treatment accords with the Hazzard definition of valvular atrial fibrillation?

דיירת בית אבות בת 83 עם דמנציה מתקדמת ו-CKD שלב 3B (eGFR 35 mL/min/1.73m²) אוכלת בצורה לקויה במשך שבועות. הצוות מדווח שהיא מצניעה אוכל בפה ואיבדה 8% ממשקל גופה. פגישות משפחה מאשרות מטרות טיפול ממוקדות נוחות. בדיקות מעבדה מראות albumin 2.9 g/dL, BUN 45 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. מהי ההתערבות המתאימה ביותר?
An older woman using diphenhydramine nightly for sleep reports worsening constipation and memory concerns. Which medication-review action addresses the risks described in Beers 2023?

An 80-year-old man with renal failure and severe hyperkalemia develops a conduction abnormality on ECG. Which treatment provides immediate myocardial protection by stabilizing the cell membrane while potassium-lowering treatment is also planned?

An older woman requires treatment for a complicated urinary tract infection. In Hazzard Table 106-6, which of the following is identified as an oral option for empiric treatment, subject to local resistance and adverse-effect considerations?
An older man with chronic pain takes tramadol and another serotonin-reuptake inhibitor. Which additional action of tramadol explains the warning about this combination?

A woman with Alzheimer disease has dangerous aggression despite assessment of reversible causes and nonpharmacologic treatment. After a risk-benefit assessment, an antipsychotic trial is chosen. Which prescribing principle follows Hazzard?
An older woman receiving long-term corticosteroids for an inflammatory condition develops muscle weakness and wasting. Which pair of effects of glucocorticoid excess is described by Hazzard?
When reassessing anticoagulation for a patient older than 75 years with atrial fibrillation, which statement about bleeding risk agrees with Hazzard?
מטופלת עם מחלת כליות כרונית מסוגלת להבין את מצבה ולהחליט, ואין מצב חירום או חריג חוקי. מוצעת לה דיאליזה ובתה תומכת בטיפול. מה נדרש לפני התחלתו?

A 76-year-old man with stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 42 mL/min/1.73 m²) and diabetes has asymptomatic bacteriuria with 100,000 CFU/mL of E. coli discovered during preoperative evaluation for cataract surgery. Urinalysis shows 10–20 WBC per high-power field and no nitrites. He has no dysuria, urgency, or fever. Which management approach fits Hazzard?

A 78-year-old man with chronic kidney disease has persistent constipation during opioid treatment despite nonpharmacologic measures and lactulose. Fecal impaction and obstruction have been excluded. Which treatment alternative is consistent with Hazzard?
An 82-year-old woman with dementia has persistent liquid fecal soiling after a period of constipation. Rectal examination finds impacted hard stool. Which interpretation best fits the source?

Lubiprostone is being considered for a patient with Parkinson disease and chronic constipation after evaluation and unsuccessful conventional treatment. By which mechanism does it promote bowel movements?

An 84-year-old nursing home resident has moderate dementia, heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35%, stage 4 chronic kidney disease with eGFR 22, and type 2 diabetes. She cannot report her medications. Staff report hard stools every 4 to 5 days despite senna 8.6 mg daily. Her abdomen is soft without masses. Which proposed addition accords with Hazzard's efficacy and renal-safety discussion?
A 79-year-old man with constipation undergoes a review of medications with anticholinergic activity. How does that activity contribute to constipation?

An older woman at high risk of constipation remains symptomatic despite lifestyle measures and appropriate trials of milder laxatives. Which treatment is supported for regular use in this refractory setting?

An independently mobile 81-year-old man has mild to moderate chronic constipation despite lifestyle changes. He drinks adequate fluids, has no suspected fecal impaction or obstruction, and has not tried laxatives. Which initial treatment fits the Hazzard stepwise approach?

A 77-year-old woman has ulcerative colitis in remission on mesalamine 800 mg three times daily. Over 3 months, she has developed straining and a bowel movement every 4 days. She also takes weekly alendronate and vitamin D, and recently started amitriptyline 10 mg for peripheral neuropathy. There is no abdominal tenderness. Which mechanism explains the constipating effect of an anticholinergic medication?
An older man with constipation has a large, hard mass of impacted stool in the rectum on examination. Which treatment sequence accords with Hazzard?

A 73-year-old woman hospitalized with a heart failure exacerbation receives intravenous furosemide 40 mg twice daily. She has had no bowel movement since admission four days ago. Her home polyethylene glycol 17 g daily was omitted. She also takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and spironolactone and eats regular meals. Potassium is 3.8, magnesium 1.9, and creatinine 1.2. Which description correctly explains the action of polyethylene glycol if it is restarted?

An 80-year-old man receiving morphine for metastatic prostate cancer has constipation despite laxative treatment. The team is considering a peripherally acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist. Which mechanism explains this drug class’s role in refractory opioid-related constipation?

An 88-year-old woman continues to strain with bowel movements despite docusate. She is at high risk of constipation complications, and milder alternatives have failed. Impaction and obstruction have been excluded. Which change accords with Hazzard?
A patient taking an opioid for chronic pain has persistent constipation despite nonpharmacologic interventions and laxatives. Which drug class is recommended at this stage?

An 82-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, diabetes, and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52) reports chronic constipation at her annual visit. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and pravastatin 20 mg daily. Increasing fiber and fluids has not helped. Her daughter reports recent use of ibuprofen 400 mg daily for joint pain. Examination and CBC are normal. Which statement about ibuprofen and constipation follows Hazzard's discussion of NSAIDs?

An 86-year-old care-home resident with Parkinson disease and severe constipation is at high risk of fecal impaction. Constipation persists after an adequate trial of lactulose and milder measures. He also has renal impairment. Which regular treatment is consistent with Hazzard?
An 84-year-old man with cognitive decline reports new constipation after a medication change. He also takes over-the-counter products. Which approach is appropriate for the initial assessment?

A 79-year-old woman with Parkinson disease recently started oxycodone and has severe constipation. Rectal examination confirms a firm impacted stool mass. Which approach addresses the current impaction and prevention of recurrence?

An 88-year-old man taking morphine has had no bowel movement for ten days and has abdominal distension and pain. Digital rectal examination finds an empty rectum. Which test is appropriate at this stage to assess fecal loading and its acute complications?

A 76-year-old woman develops dry mouth, constipation, and sleepiness after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. Alongside assessment and treatment of constipation, which principle should guide review of this drug under Beers 2023?

An 81-year-old man with advanced chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, and recently diagnosed colon cancer has severe constipation and cramping abdominal pain after chemotherapy. He takes ondansetron, aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. Vital signs are stable; the abdomen is distended with hyperactive bowel sounds, and abdominal imaging shows fecal loading without obstruction. Which laxative does Hazzard advise against because of its greater adverse-effect risk in older adults?

A bedbound 92-year-old woman has overflow fecal incontinence. A large, hard rectal stool mass is palpable, and treatment causes pain. She has advanced chronic kidney disease. The goal is relief of discomfort. Which approach is appropriate?

A 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease and benign prostatic enlargement develops constipation, confusion, and urinary retention after starting tolterodine. Which combination supports concern about a drug effect?
An older woman with dementia and constipation takes verapamil and an iron supplement. How should these medications be considered during the constipation assessment?

An 80-year-old woman in rehabilitation after a hip fracture has constipation and receives an opioid and lorazepam for anxiety. Constipation is being evaluated and treated separately. Why should lorazepam also be reassessed?

A 78-year-old man with dementia takes medications that contribute to constipation. He has had no bowel movement for 12 days, and rectal examination reveals a large, firm stool mass. There are no peritoneal signs, and medication review has begun. Which approach is appropriate for clearing the rectal impaction?

An 83-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease and a creatinine clearance of 35 mL/min has persistent constipation despite milder treatments. She asks about regular laxative treatment. Which statement agrees with Hazzard?
An older man with Alzheimer disease develops confusion, dry mouth, and constipation after starting oxybutynin. Which explanation is consistent with the drug effects listed in Hazzard?

An 86-year-old resident with constipation and a defecatory disorder has significant cognitive impairment. He has difficulty learning instructions and remembering practice exercises. Which limitation is particularly relevant when considering biofeedback?
A 77-year-old woman with long-standing untreated hypothyroidism develops altered mental status after receiving an opioid. Which clinical combination supports myxedema coma?

An older man with chronic kidney disease has persistent constipation despite simple measures and docusate. Fecal impaction and obstruction have been excluded. Which oral treatment is an appropriate escalation according to Hazzard?

A 79-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease and recurrent UTIs has worsening constipation despite lactulose 30 mL daily. She has had no bowel movement for five days and reports abdominal pain. Examination shows abdominal distension and a large, firm rectal fecal impaction. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and prophylactic trimethoprim; creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Before inserting rectal enemas or suppositories, what does Hazzard recommend for the firm impaction?

An 87-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia presents from a nursing facility with acute confusion and agitation. He has had no bowel movement for 10 days despite daily docusate. His abdomen is markedly distended and tympanitic; radiographs show dilated bowel loops, air-fluid levels, and a large rectosigmoid stool burden. Blood pressure is 95/60, heart rate 110, potassium 3.2, creatinine 1.8 (baseline 1.2), and white blood cell count 14,000. Which agent does Hazzard specifically advise against in older people because it can promote colonic pseudo-obstruction?

A 92-year-old woman with COPD requiring home oxygen, heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and chronic pain from spinal stenosis takes sustained-release morphine 15 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 5 mg daily. She reports straining for 30 minutes and passing small, hard stools every 3–4 days. She has fallen twice in the past month while straining on the toilet. A suppository is being considered for rectal outlet delay. Which initial choice and timing follow Hazzard?

An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18) is brought to the emergency department after two days of unusual behavior. His daughter recalls an unnamed constipation medicine. He is confused and has asterixis. Results are sodium 138, potassium 4.1, creatinine 1.4, and magnesium 4.8 mEq/L (laboratory reference range 1.5–2.5). His other medications are donepezil, memantine, and atorvastatin. Which statement about laxative safety supports investigating magnesium hydroxide exposure?

A 77-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, hypertension, and osteoarthritis attends routine follow-up. Her daughter reports frequent liquid stool soiling despite complaints of constipation. Medications include amlodipine 5 mg, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. Digital rectal examination reveals a large mass of hard stool in the rectal vault with liquid stool leaking around it. Lawton-Brody assessment shows new difficulty shopping and preparing meals. What is the preferred initial approach?

An 85-year-old man is in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a hip fracture. He has Parkinson disease and benign prostatic hyperplasia and takes carbidopa/levodopa, tamsulosin, oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, and ferrous sulfate. He has had no bowel movement for 7 days despite daily lactulose. Abdominal radiography shows a moderate colonic stool burden, and creatinine clearance is 38 mL/min. Which option is supported for ongoing laxative treatment?

An older woman receiving an opioid has constipation. Examination identifies a large, firm rectal impaction, without peritoneal signs or suspected perforation. According to Hazzard, what should precede insertion of an enema or suppository?

An 83-year-old man with advanced COPD on home oxygen at 3 L/min, moderate dementia, and failure to thrive is hospitalized with aspiration pneumonia. His family requests palliative care and a do-not-resuscitate order. He develops severe constipation and abdominal distension causing respiratory distress. Digital rectal examination finds an empty rectum, but abdominal radiography shows extensive colonic stool loading. His QTc is 480 ms. Which approach to the constipation is supported by Hazzard?

A 76-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis takes prednisone 7.5 mg daily. Three weeks after starting amitriptyline 25 mg for peripheral neuropathy, she develops hard stools every four to five days with straining. She also takes methotrexate, folic acid, and omeprazole. Examination shows mild abdominal distension and stool in the rectal vault. Which strategy addresses a possible anticholinergic medication contribution while considering an alternative for neuropathic pain?

An older woman with constipation and abdominal distension has an empty rectum on examination. An abdominal radiograph shows fecal loading in the ascending and transverse colon without acute obstruction. What treatment implication does this finding have?

A 72-year-old man with newly diagnosed metastatic pancreatic cancer started sustained-release morphine 30 mg twice daily for pain. Two weeks later, pain is controlled, but he has had no bowel movement for six days despite docusate 200 mg twice daily. Examination shows mild abdominal distention and a moderate amount of stool in the rectal vault. His goals include maintaining quality of life and activity. Which change is supported for treating his opioid-related constipation?

An 80-year-old woman with limited mobility cannot safely reach the toilet at night. Constipation treatment and medication review are already underway. Which environmental intervention directly addresses toilet access?

A 91-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, dysphagia requiring a pureed diet, and recurrent aspiration pneumonia has severe constipation. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, pramipexole, and lansoprazole. He spends an hour straining on the toilet. Examination shows normal anal tone but impaired coordination of pelvic floor relaxation. Lactulose, suppositories, and enemas have not helped. His creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Which intervention directly targets the pelvic floor coordination problem?
An 82-year-old woman with CKD and constipation asks about magnesium citrate. Which safety consideration matches Hazzard?

A 78-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer (PSA 156 ng/mL) is being considered for docetaxel. He lives alone, has difficulty managing finances, and has fallen twice in the past month. BMI is 19.2 kg/m². He takes tamsulosin, amlodipine, and trazodone for sleep. Hemoglobin is 10.2 g/dL, albumin 2.8 g/dL, and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (eGFR 35 mL/min). Which assessment best addresses the aging-related vulnerabilities relevant to chemotherapy planning?

An 81-year-old woman with newly diagnosed breast cancer is admitted with delirium after her first cyclophosphamide-based chemotherapy cycle. Her daughter reports poor intake and slowing over the preceding week. Vital signs are stable. Sodium is 128 mEq/L, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL from a baseline of 0.9, WBC 2.8 K/microliter, and Mini-Cog 1/5. For future care planning, which use of comprehensive geriatric assessment matches the multidisciplinary intervention reported to reduce chemotherapy toxicity?
An older woman takes gabapentin and has a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min. Which treatment adjustment matches the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

An 84-year-old woman with colon cancer is three days after hemicolectomy. She pulls out her Foley catheter and becomes agitated when staff try to replace it. CAM findings include acute onset, inattention, and disorganized thinking. She takes donepezil 10 mg for mild dementia; electrolytes are normal and hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL. Review confirms no ongoing indication for the catheter. Which step addresses this source of immobilization?
A 76-year-old man meets the Fried operational criteria for exhaustion and slow walking. Which additional finding belongs to the phenotype and could complete three criteria?

A woman cannot meet her nutritional needs by eating, but her gastrointestinal tract is suitable for feeding. Which potential advantage of enteral rather than parenteral nutrition is described in Hazzard?

An 82-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer has lost 15% of his body weight over two months. His ECOG performance status is 2, and the oncologist recommends FOLFIRINOX. Assessment shows low grip strength of 18 kg, slow gait speed of 0.6 m/s, and a Mini Nutritional Assessment score of 19. Under the EWGSOP2 approach described in Hazzard, which additional assessment estimates the muscle-mass component needed to support a sarcopenia diagnosis?

אישה בת 75 עם AML שוקלת כימותרפיה. היא מבינה את המידע ויכולה לקבל החלטה, ואומרת: "אני רוצה לחיות עד סיום הלימודים של נכדתי, אבל איני רוצה לסבול." כבר נמסרה לה התועלת הצפויה. איזו שאלה תברר באופן הישיר ביותר את האיזון שהיא מבקשת בין הארכת חיים לנטל הטיפול?

An 80-year-old man with prostate cancer develops urinary retention. PSA is 28 ng/mL and postvoid residual is 450 mL. He takes tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, terazosin 5 mg for hypertension, finasteride 5 mg, and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily for urgency. BP is 108/68 seated and 92/58 standing. Which medication change removes an anticholinergic bladder relaxant that can contribute to retention?

A 78-year-old woman has taken metoclopramide daily for several months for nausea unrelated to gastroparesis. She develops repetitive involuntary mouth and tongue movements. Which change follows the 2023 AGS Beers warning about this prolonged exposure?
An 81-year-old man has severe hyperkalemia with bradycardia and marked conduction delay. What immediate effect does Hazzard attribute to intravenous calcium gluconate in this situation?

A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia becomes agitated while being prepared for cancer treatment. She has no major depression, psychosis, or behavior that endangers herself or staff. Calming interventions have not yet been tried. Which initial approach is appropriate according to Hazzard?

An older adult taking metformin is hospitalized with severe diarrhea, dehydration, and acute deterioration in kidney function. How should metformin be managed during this acute illness according to Hazzard?

A 77-year-old woman has undergone breast-conserving surgery for a small, hormone receptor-positive, node-negative tumor. She plans endocrine therapy and is considering omission of radiation. What oncologic trade-off does Hazzard describe for appropriately selected patients?
An 85-year-old man with fatigue and weakness is being evaluated for suspected adrenal insufficiency. Which distinction between primary and secondary adrenal insufficiency is described in Hazzard?
An older woman newly diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer has symptoms and is continuing oncologic assessment and treatment. When does Hazzard recommend considering palliative care?

A 79-year-old man has localized prostate cancer (Gleason 3+4, PSA 8.2), type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.8%), and stage 3b CKD (eGFR 42; Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38 mL/min). He uses a walker after a recent hip fracture and has ECOG performance status 2. His medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, and alendronate 70 mg weekly. Estimated life expectancy is 6 years. After discussion, he chooses to defer cancer treatment until symptomatic disease develops, rather than plan delayed curative treatment. Which strategy describes this choice?

An older woman has had lumpectomy for a small, hormone receptor-positive, node-negative breast cancer. She plans to take endocrine therapy and is discussing omission of breast irradiation. In the selected population described by Hazzard, what difference is expected compared with adding irradiation?

A man with prostate cancer develops new, severe back pain, raising concern for spinal cord compression. He has no neurologic deficit on examination. What initial approach is appropriate according to Hazzard?
What does comprehensive geriatric assessment add to treatment planning for an older woman with breast cancer?

An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced dementia and breast cancer metastatic to bone presents with two days of shouting, agitation, food refusal, and pulling at her clothes. She is nonverbal at baseline and grimaces during abdominal palpation. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, heart rate 88, and blood pressure 142/78. She receives memantine 10 mg twice daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. Which approach best addresses the acute behavioral change?
A patient with asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia receives conservative-management advice. Which approach accords with Hazzard?
An 85-year-old woman with severe cancer pain and renal impairment needs an opioid regimen adjusted. Which pharmacokinetic principle should guide dose selection and monitoring?

אישה בת 73 עם סרטן שד בשלב מוקדם מסרבת לניתוח ואומרת: 'חייתי חיים טובים.' היא עצמאית בכל ה-ADLs, הולכת 2 מיילים ביום, ומתנדבת בכנסייה. התרופה היחידה שלה היא lisinopril 5mg. MMSE 30/30. בתה טוענת שהיא בדיכאון ודורשת הערכה פסיכיאטרית. איזה גישה היא המתאימה ביותר?
An older adult taking an opioid has undergone clearance of a fecal impaction. Under Hazzard’s stepwise approach, what ongoing treatment helps prevent recurrence?
A woman with breast cancer and bone metastases asks why denosumab or a bisphosphonate has been proposed. What role does Hazzard describe for this treatment?
An older patient has suspected opioid overdose with respiratory depression. Naloxone is being considered during emergency treatment. What is its purpose?

A 75-year-old woman completed adjuvant chemotherapy for breast cancer three months ago. She has increasing difficulty rising from a chair and climbing stairs and fell last week. Her BMI is 19, grip strength 14 kg, and gait speed 0.6 m/s. She takes anastrozole 1 mg daily and calcium/vitamin D. Which rehabilitation principle follows Hazzard's discussion of maintaining and restoring muscle mass and strength?

A 79-year-old man taking a diuretic presents after reduced intake. He has weight loss, orthostatic hypotension, and hyponatremia. Evaluation establishes hypovolemia without pulmonary congestion or edema. Which treatment addresses this mechanism?

An 81-year-old woman treated for ER-positive/PR-positive breast cancer 5 years ago has new back pain and weight loss. MRI shows multiple vertebral metastases, and biopsy confirms recurrent breast cancer. She has mild cognitive impairment, lives in assisted living, and has a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min. She declines further chemotherapy but is willing to discuss endocrine treatment. Her metastases are not rapidly progressive or life-threatening. Which approach accords with Hazzard?

An 82-year-old man with localized low-risk prostate cancer asks about active surveillance and the possibility of later curative treatment. He has moderate COPD, diabetes with neuropathy, polypharmacy including gabapentin and oxybutynin, recurrent falls with declining daily function, and reduced renal function. Which description of active surveillance agrees with Hazzard?
After radical prostatectomy, a patient's PSA does not fall to an undetectable level. Which evaluation does Hazzard recommend?
An older man with an enlarged prostate and lower urinary tract symptoms asks about finasteride because he wants rapid relief. Which description of its action and onset agrees with Hazzard?
According to Hazzard, which statement describes the use of prostate brachytherapy in relation to disease risk and prostate size?
A 77-year-old man is undergoing active surveillance for low-risk prostate cancer. A repeat biopsy now shows primary Gleason pattern 4. Which management change does this finding support?
An older adult with castration-resistant prostate cancer is being considered for enzalutamide. Which history calls for the specific neurologic caution described in Hazzard?
A 76-year-old man with osteoporosis following androgen-deprivation therapy is considering denosumab. What is its mechanism of action?

An 84-year-old man with a urinary catheter is hospitalized with complicated UTI and sepsis. Culture identifies a ceftriaxone-susceptible organism, he has no allergy to the drug, and his condition still requires hospitalization. Which option is appropriate during this severe phase?

A 79-year-old man with locally advanced prostate cancer has received leuprolide for 18 months. He reports progressive fatigue, poor appetite, and loss of interest in woodworking. His PHQ-9 score is 14; his wife died 8 months ago. Testosterone is below 20 ng/dL and creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. If depression is confirmed after excluding other causes, which drug belongs to the first-line group described in Hazzard's cancer chapter?

An 83-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate cancer and extensive bone metastases has severe back pain despite morphine 30 mg every 4 hours. Pain prevents independent transfers; he previously walked with a walker. MRI shows multilevel vertebral metastases without cord compression. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL. His severe pain is localized to one spinal area. Which basis for palliative radiation referral accords with Hazzard?
A 77-year-old man is starting androgen-deprivation therapy for prostate cancer. He asks how treatment affects bone health. Which approach is consistent with Hazzard?
A patient receiving antiresorptive treatment underwent a tooth extraction. An area of exposed, necrotic jaw bone has now failed to heal for ten weeks. Which complication matches this finding?
Watchful waiting is discussed with a man who has prostate cancer. Which principle defines this approach in Hazzard?

An older man with high-risk prostate cancer is asymptomatic and has a limited life expectancy. He and his team are considering watchful waiting. What distinguishes this approach from active surveillance intended to permit delayed curative treatment?

A man with lower urinary tract symptoms has not improved with empiric treatment. He has low urinary flow and residual urine, but bladder outlet obstruction and impaired detrusor contractility remain possible. Which test is the standard for diagnosing obstruction?
According to the PACIFIC trial description in Hazzard, what was concluded about durvalumab after disease control with chemoradiation in unresectable stage III lung cancer?

A 78-year-old woman who has never smoked has stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, brain metastases, and an EGFR L858R mutation. She takes amlodipine, metformin, and simvastatin, has reduced renal function, and lives independently but has stopped driving because of mild cognitive impairment. Which initial treatment is supported by the FLAURA results described in Hazzard, including improved overall survival and efficacy in CNS metastases?

An 84-year-old man with early-stage non-small-cell lung cancer is medically inoperable because of severe lung disease. The team proposes stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). Which description captures its technical advantage over conventional radiation in Hazzard?
An older woman recovers slowly after resection of stage II NSCLC. What does the delayed recovery mean for consideration of adjuvant chemotherapy, according to Hazzard?

A patient with cancer and diagnosed adrenal insufficiency is clinically stable and is not under acute physiologic stress. The patient receives regular hydrocortisone replacement. Which timing principle does Hazzard emphasize?
A medication review before cancer treatment identifies oxybutynin use. Which statement reflects Beers 2023 regarding its cognitive effects among bladder antimuscarinics?
In which population was durvalumab studied in the PACIFIC trial as described in Hazzard?

A 76-year-old woman taking sertraline and hydrochlorothiazide presents with new confusion and a seizure. Serum sodium is 118 mEq/L, serum osmolality is low, and urine is concentrated; she is clinically euvolemic. Alongside evaluation and treatment of contributing causes, which sodium-directed treatment should be started according to Hazzard?
An 80-year-old patient receiving pembrolizumab develops severe colitis attributed to immune-related toxicity. Which treatment principle does Hazzard describe for severe immune-related adverse events?

A 78-year-old man with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer completed concurrent chemoradiation 3 months ago. He had an excellent response, with dose reductions for neutropenia. He remains independent, but his daughter reports new forgetfulness. Creatinine clearance is 40 mL/min and the latest brain MRI is normal. During discussion of prophylactic cranial irradiation, which potential treatment effect warrants attention according to Hazzard?
Before treatment for lung cancer, grip strength is found to be below the reference values for sex and population. How should this finding be interpreted in the evaluation of sarcopenia?

An 83-year-old man with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer is undergoing systemic treatment planning. An ALK molecular alteration has been identified. What is the significance of molecular testing for treatment selection according to Hazzard?

אישה בת 79 עם NSCLC שלב IV (PD-L1 5%, ללא מוטציות) שמתקדמת לאחר קו ראשון של carboplatin/pemetrexed/pembrolizumab. היא זקוקה לסיוע של הליכון לאחר שפיתחה נוירופתיה היקפית. מצב תפקודי הוא ECOG 2. היא שואלת על אפשרויות קו שני. בתה רוצה 'שייעשה הכל' אך המטופלת נראית מהססת. איזה גישה מתייחסת בצורה הטובה ביותר למטרות טיפול?
גבר עם דמנציה קלה וסרטן אומר שהוא סומך על בנו. לפני קביעה שאינו מסוגל לתת הסכמה לטיפול רפואי, איזה בירור רלוונטי לפי חוק זכויות החולה?
For a patient receiving osimertinib, which pair appears in Hazzard’s table of adverse effects of targeted lung cancer treatment?

An 84-year-old man with resected colon cancer walks with a walker after recent falls. Adjuvant treatment containing oxaliplatin is being discussed. Which combination of consequences of oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy does Hazzard identify in older adults with colon cancer?
A 78-year-old woman without symptoms or a history of adenomas is discussing colorectal cancer screening. What should be established before choosing fecal immunochemical testing (FIT)?
An 81-year-old man with localized colon cancer is referred for resection. Which finding from studies summarized in Hazzard informs discussion of the hospital and surgical approach?

A 79-year-old woman treated with oxaliplatin for colon cancer develops peripheral neuropathy, falls, and difficulty buttoning her clothes. Which geriatric consequence of neuropathy is relevant when reviewing further treatment?

בן 86 בישראל לאחר כריתת סרטן מעי גס שוקל טיפול משלים פומי. הוא מסוגל להבין ולקבל החלטה בעזרת הסבר נגיש. הוסברו מטרת הטיפול, התועלת והסיכונים, אך לא הוצגו אפשרויות אחרות. מה חסר להשלמת המידע לפי סעיף 13 לחוק זכויות החולה?
According to Hazzard, which rationale supports considering a shorter duration of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant chemotherapy in an older adult with colon cancer?

An 83-year-old woman with localized colorectal cancer, heart failure, and functional limitations is being assessed for treatment. No urgent intervention is currently needed. Which basis for decision-making follows the principles described for older adults with gastrointestinal malignancy?
A 76-year-old man with diabetes taking metformin develops a severe acute illness with tissue hypoperfusion around the time of surgery. What is the main reason to avoid metformin in this situation?
An older woman with localized rectal cancer asks about the standard surgical procedure described in Hazzard. Which answer matches that description?
An 82-year-old man with metastatic colorectal cancer is considering capecitabine. Which statement is supported by Hazzard without assuming that it is superior to every alternative regimen for him?
A woman has undergone complete removal of a colonic adenoma. How does this history affect her risk classification when planning surveillance according to Hazzard?

An older adult with metastatic colorectal cancer has uncontrollable bleeding from the primary tumor. Which feature is an indication for resection of the primary tumor in advanced disease according to Hazzard?

A 79-year-old woman previously treated for colorectal cancer has a recurrence confined to a solitary resectable liver metastasis. Her surgical assessment is favorable. Which feature supports discussing a curative-intent resection?
An 81-year-old man with locally invasive T4 rectal cancer receives chemoradiation as part of a plan that includes surgery. What benefit is described for chemoradiation before or after surgery?

A 77-year-old woman develops acute confusion after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for colon cancer. She tries to pull out her Foley catheter and does not recognize her daughter. She was independent before surgery. Her vital signs are stable, renal function has worsened, and urinalysis is negative. The Foley is no longer clinically indicated. Alongside evaluation of medical contributors, which measure follows the recommended nonpharmacologic approach?
For a basal cell carcinoma located in a low-risk area, which combination of life expectancy and additional lesion risk does Hazzard describe for discussing active surveillance?

A 79-year-old woman has a new 8-mm pigmented lesion on her shoulder with asymmetry, irregular borders, and multiple colors. It is suspicious for melanoma and can be completely removed in a minor procedure. Which approach is appropriate for the initial histologic diagnosis?
An 88-year-old man with an isolated actinic keratosis on his scalp is treated with liquid nitrogen. Which mechanism explains destruction of the lesion according to Hazzard?

A 76-year-old woman presents for Mohs surgery for a 1.2-cm basal cell carcinoma on the tip of her nose. She reports increasing difficulty managing her finances and has missed two appointments. Her daughter confirms that she has recently forgotten to pay bills. Her MMSE score is 22/30. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Which statement about Mohs surgery in older adults is supported by Hazzard?

An older man with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma has been assessed and is a suitable surgical candidate. The lesion is classified as high risk. Which approach does Hazzard describe as the usual treatment for this risk category?
An older woman receiving immunosuppressive treatment is diagnosed with Merkel cell carcinoma. Which statement about this disease is supported by Hazzard?

An older adult has cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma with perineural involvement. After assessing the patient's overall condition, the team discusses local treatment of this high-risk lesion. Which approach is described in Hazzard?

אישה עם דמנציה מתקדמת בישראל נזקקת להחלטה לגבי בירור נגע עור חשוד. מונה לה אפוטרופוס. היא אינה מסוגלת להבין את ההחלטה, אין הנחיות מקדימות בנושא, אך ידועות העדפותיה הקודמות לגבי בירור כזה. מה ינחה את האפוטרופוס לפי סעיף 67ו(ב)(2)?
What is the mechanism of photodynamic therapy for actinic keratoses according to Hazzard?

A 78-year-old woman has cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma arising in a chronic heel wound. The lesion is classified as high risk. Which treatment approach does Hazzard describe for high-risk keratinocyte carcinoma?

גבר בן 83 מגיע עם seborrheic dermatitis חדש ופיתוח מהיר של מאות seborrheic keratoses במשך 3 חודשים (סימן Leser-Trélat). הוא מדווח על ירידה של 20 פאונד במשקל וסיפוק מוקדם. CBC מראה Hgb 9.2 g/dL עם MCV 72. Ferritin הוא 18 ng/mL. Upper endoscopy מגלה adenocarcinoma גסטרי. הוא שואל לגבי הסרת ה-keratoses המגרדות. מה התגובה המתאימה ביותר?
A 79-year-old woman has a lesion diagnosed as a keratoacanthoma. She asks why excision is being considered when such lesions can regress. Which explanation is consistent with Hazzard?

An older patient with limited life expectancy has chosen active surveillance for an asymptomatic, low-risk basal cell carcinoma after discussion. The lesion is in a low-risk area and there are no additional risk factors. What does this surveillance pathway include?

A man with high-risk basal cell carcinoma of the face is unsuitable for surgery after individualized assessment. The lesion is neither small nor superficial. Which alternative does Hazzard describe for a patient with a contraindication to surgery?

An 82-year-old woman has biopsy-confirmed BCC on the nose, classified as high risk. Assessment finds her fit for surgery, able to understand the decision, and supported for wound care. Which local treatment is generally appropriate for this high-risk lesion?

A 78-year-old man with iron-deficiency anemia is suitable for oral iron replacement. He tolerates oral therapy and does not need urgent transfusion. Which initial strategy and rationale match Hazzard?

An 84-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 24) and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three she develops acute confusion, visual hallucinations, and agitation; the CAM is positive. She pulls at an indwelling urinary catheter that is no longer medically needed. She is receiving levofloxacin, acetaminophen, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. Which initial intervention best follows Hazzard’s nonpharmacologic approach?

A 76-year-old man has gait disturbance and paresthesias and is found to have vitamin B12 deficiency. His blood count shows neither anemia nor macrocytosis. How should the absent hematologic findings be interpreted?
A patient with chronic hemolytic anemia is asymptomatic at a baseline hemoglobin of 6 g/dL. A target of 7 g/dL is being considered. What consequence does the example in Hazzard describe?

A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis develops fatigue and exertional dyspnea after starting meloxicam for knee pain. Hemoglobin is 8.2 g/dL, MCV 78 fL, ferritin 18 ng/mL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL from 1.1, and eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m². Stool testing is positive for blood and colonoscopy shows a bleeding diverticulum. After the acute bleed is treated, which analgesic principle follows Hazzard's discussion of safer prescribing for osteoarthritis?
How should treatment suitability be assessed in an older adult with acute myeloid leukemia and functional decline?
Erythropoietin treatment is being considered for a patient with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. Which combination is associated with a greater likelihood of benefit?

An 80-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome has transfusion-related iron overload. Before deciding about iron chelation, the team assesses disease risk, continuing transfusion needs, and expected survival. Which combination matches the Hazzard recommendation for initiating chelation?
A 75-year-old woman with a serious infection requires antibiotic treatment. Which initial dosing principle for older adults follows Hazzard?

An 83-year-old man with chronic lymphocytic leukemia develops anemia. Before deciding on treatment, which pair of investigations does Hazzard recommend to help distinguish hemolysis from decreased bone marrow production?
Initial testing has not identified the cause of anemia in an older woman. When is the term unexplained anemia of the elderly appropriate?

An 81-year-old woman with previously unevaluated anemia presents for an initial assessment. There is no specific suspicion of a hematologic malignancy. Which group of tests belongs in the initial work-up described in Hazzard?
An older adult with a myeloproliferative neoplasm and polycythemia is being assessed for thrombosis risk. Which relationship between polycythemia and thrombosis is described in Hazzard?

An 85-year-old woman with mild dementia and osteoporosis has undergone repair of a hip fracture. She is stable, has no symptoms attributed to anemia, and has a hemoglobin of 9.2 g/dL. Which principle should guide a postoperative transfusion decision in the perioperative-care chapter?
A patient with anemia due to chronic kidney disease starts erythropoietin treatment. Iron stores were adequate before treatment. Which change requires monitoring during therapy?

A 78-year-old man with CLL takes ibrutinib 420 mg/day. He also has hypertension treated with lisinopril 10 mg and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 45); he takes aspirin 81 mg. He presents with three weeks of progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea and five days of dark stools. He is pale, with BP 128/78, heart rate 96, no orthostatic changes, and no lymphadenopathy. Hemoglobin is 6.8 g/dL (baseline 11.2), MCV 82, platelets 165,000, WBC 42,000 with 85% lymphocytes, and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (baseline 1.4). He has received one unit of packed red cells and is hemodynamically stable. Which statement about ibrutinib is relevant to reviewing his bleeding risk?

An 84-year-old woman presents with fatigue, macrocytic anemia, and functional decline. Her vitamin B12 level is 189 pg/mL, her folate level is normal, and no other clear explanation has been found. Which approach agrees with Table 30-7 in Hazzard?
An older patient with multiple myeloma and renal insufficiency is about to receive lenalidomide. Which approach to dosing is consistent with Hazzard?

An 81-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia is admitted from assisted living for pneumonia. On day three, she becomes disoriented and tries to leave. She previously managed basic ADLs independently but now needs dressing assistance. She takes donepezil 10 mg, sertraline 50 mg, and IV ceftriaxone. Vital signs are stable; WBC is 14,000, creatinine 0.9, and electrolytes normal. While assessing acute precipitants, which initial symptom-management approach fits Hazzard?

A 77-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and newly diagnosed AML is being considered for intensive induction chemotherapy. His wife reports more frequent falls and a missed bill payment. He appears frail and has reduced grip strength and slow gait. Which assessment addresses these functional and cognitive concerns together when planning cancer treatment?
A woman with CLL develops anemia. The team wants to distinguish hemolysis from decreased bone marrow production. Which tests does Hazzard recommend obtaining for this distinction?

A 76-year-old man who has received immunosuppressive treatment presents with pneumonia. When choosing empirical therapy, why is it important to determine the type, intensity, and duration of immunosuppression?

בישראל, חולה בגירה הוגדרה כדין כחולה הנוטה למות שאינה בעלת כשרות. אין הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות, החלטת מיופה כוח או החלטת ועדה לפי סעיף 5(ב). בתה, שהוכרה כאדם קרוב, מצהירה במפורש שאמה אינה רוצה להוסיף לחיות. כיצד יש להשתמש בהצהרה בבירור רצון החולה לפי סעיף 5(ג)?
A 78-year-old man receiving acyclovir develops a decline in renal function. During medication review, which variable does Hazzard’s antiviral treatment table specify for adjusting acyclovir dosing?

An 82-year-old woman living at home has recurrent falls and uses a walker. She also has smoldering myeloma and moderate aortic stenosis. Which pair contains two interventions described in Hazzard as effective for fall prevention in community-dwelling older adults at high risk?
A 75-year-old man with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia needs a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. Which consideration should guide treatment selection in an older adult?

An older woman with low-risk MDS is transfusion dependent. Cytogenetic testing shows an isolated deletion of the long arm of chromosome 5. Which treatment is the standard approach described for this subgroup?

A 79-year-old man has severe pain from a new vertebral compression fracture. There is no cord compression or described neuropathic pain, and the cause of the fracture is still being investigated. Nonopioid therapy has provided inadequate relief. After assessment, an opioid trial is chosen. Which initiation approach matches Hazzard?

A 77-year-old woman with AML in remission after venetoclax/azacitidine, diabetes, and depression has stopped driving and cooking and sleeps much of the day. Her MMSE is 26/30. She takes prophylactic acyclovir, metformin, and long-standing sertraline 100 mg daily. Examination shows psychomotor slowing, and her CBC is normal. If hypothyroidism is being evaluated as a possible contributor, which initial assessment does Hazzard recommend?
In a patient with polycythemia vera, which description of thrombotic risk agrees with Hazzard?

A 79-year-old man with longstanding untreated hypothyroidism becomes confused after cold exposure. Hypothermia, bradycardia, and hypoventilation raise concern for myxedema crisis. Alongside supportive care and thyroid hormone replacement, how should adrenal reserve be addressed?

An 84-year-old woman is undergoing a separate evaluation for anemia and fatigue. Two tests 3 months apart show an unchanged TSH of 5.8 mIU/L with normal free T4. Which thyroid recommendation is consistent with Hazzard?
An older adult with severe hypothermia has persistent cardiac arrhythmias after initial stabilization. Which temperature-management approach follows Hazzard?

An 81-year-old woman develops acute confusion while taking several psychoactive medications, including regular lorazepam. Recent medication changes and other medical contributors have not yet been assessed. How should the medication component of the evaluation be approached?

A 77-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia is minimally responsive on morning rounds. Her core temperature is 31°C, blood pressure 85/50 mm Hg, and heart rate 45 beats/min.
